indicators.description: Plots the Ulcer Index, squaring each bar's percentage drawdown from the running high across a 14-bar window and rooting the averaged result, as a gradient-filled line with a dashed alert threshold at 5.0 and an optional Drawdown % column plot. Four alerts cover threshold crosses in both directions, fresh drawdowns and reclaimed highs, for traders who define risk as time spent underwater.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Ultimate AMD Indicator
indicators.description: Automates Smart Money cycle detection: it boxes accumulation ranges, flags the manipulation breakout that traps traders, then tracks distribution as the real move unfolds, with fair value gaps and their inverted counterparts mapped alongside. ATR filtering and collision control keep the chart readable. For SMC traders hunting structural reversals.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Ultimate Opening Range Breakout
indicators.description: Turns the opening range into a full trading framework: BULL and BEAR BREAK signals graded by volume, expansion targets sized to the range, an ATR trailing stop with a five-setting optimizer, and a dashboard logging historical target hit rates. A built-in volume profile reveals the point of control behind each break. Built for traders of the market open.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Ultimate Oscillator
indicators.description: The Ultimate Oscillator blends buying pressure relative to true range across three timeframes into a single weighted momentum reading bounded between 0 and 100. Defaults are the classic 7, 14, and 28 period lengths with the usual 4/2/1 weighting. This is the standard implementation of Larry Williams' Ultimate Oscillator.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Ultimate RSI
indicators.description: The Ultimate RSI reworks the classic Relative Strength Index into a trend-first oscillator, weighting price changes by the rolling range so overbought and oversold readings arrive sooner and hold through strong moves. With four smoothing methods, a signal line, and colored trend zones, it suits trend followers who find the standard RSI too noisy.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Ultimate Smoother
indicators.description: Plots John Ehlers' Ultimate Smoother, a low-pass price filter with essentially zero lag in its passband, colored by slope with a 20-bar critical period by default. An optional 50-period slow companion turns it into a crossover pair with a trend-colored fill, and six alerts cover price crosses, slope turns and companion crossovers.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Unfinished Auction
indicators.description: Audits each completed session, daily by default, for highs and lows that ended without an excess tail, flagging stacked, heavily traded or closing-bell extremes as unfinished reference levels that extend until price repairs them. A dashboard ranks open references by distance and tracks the share of recent extremes left unfinished, with alerts on new and repaired levels.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Universal Signal Backtester
indicators.description: The Universal Signal Backtester turns any signal into measurable results: predefined moving average crosses, crossovers of two external sources, or triggers piped in from your own scripts. It manages up to three take-profit and stop-loss levels, simulates spread and commission, and grades everything on a dashboard with Sharpe ratio, profit factor, and a time-based heatmap.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Unreached Highs/Lows Oscillator
indicators.description: The Unreached Highs/Lows Oscillator counts the share of recent highs and lows that price has left untested and plots each side as a normalized 0-100 line. Sustained readings beyond the 80/20 thresholds confirm directional control, mid-range values flag ranging conditions, and sudden drops expose breakouts as old levels are reclaimed.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Up/down Volume
indicators.description: Up/down Volume splits each bar's volume by close direction and displays the streams as mirrored columns, a net-volume oscillator, or the running Cumulative Volume Index, with smoothed averages (default 20-bar SMA) overlaying every mode. Gradient columns brighten on unusually heavy bars. For traders who want to see which side the volume is actually on.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Up/down Volume Ratio
indicators.description: Up/down Volume Ratio divides volume traded on advancing bars by volume traded on declining bars, read against a 1.0 balance level: the classic 50-bar screening construction, plus session totals and an intrabar tick split. A dashboard reports the ratio, its bias, and the up-volume share. For traders screening accumulation the growth-stock way.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Upside/downside Tasuki Gap
indicators.description: Detects upside and downside Tasuki gaps: two trend candles split by a real gap, then an opposite candle pressing into the gap without closing it, filtered by a 50-period SMA trend context. Each pattern draws its unfilled gap as an extending zone with a confirmation level at the second candle's extreme, and eight alerts track detection, confirmation, retests and fills.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Upthrust
indicators.description: Upthrust frames mature trading ranges from clustered swing highs and labels failed breakouts above resistance: UT and UTAD marks with graded tooltips covering ATR penetration, volume effort, and reclaim speed, plus secondary-test and invalidation marks. Defaults: swing length 10, 0.5 ATR tolerance, 3-bar acceptance window. For Wyckoff-minded traders hunting trapped buyers.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Upthrust After Distribution
indicators.description: Detects the Wyckoff UTAD: after a 2-ATR advance stalls into an established, boundary-tested range, a late break above resistance that fails back inside within 5 bars is labeled, with the UTAD high as invalidation and a projection one range height below support. Secondary tests, signs of weakness and refuting breakouts are labeled, with six alerts across the sequence.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: V-top/V-bottom
indicators.description: Detects V-tops and V-bottoms from exhaustion evidence: an accelerating final leg of at least 3 ATRs whose extreme bar prints a volume spike, wide-range bar or failing gap becomes a candidate tip, confirmed when the return leg retraces 80% of it at comparable speed. Confirmed Vs draw reference levels and a first-pullback signal, with eight alerts from climax to invalidation.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Valid BOS Pullback
indicators.description: The Valid BOS Pullback indicator identifies trend continuations by filtering standard Break of Structure events through a retest requirement. It detects initial breakouts and waits for the price to pull back to the structural level before confirming the continuation if a new extreme is reached. This process helps traders avoid false breakouts and focus on higher probability continuation patterns by ensuring the structural level acts as support or resistance after the initial breach.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Value Area Reversion Signals
indicators.description: The Value Area Reversion Signals indicator helps traders identify potential market reversals by analyzing volume distribution. It generates an anchored volume profile, highlighting the Point of Control and Value Area. The indicator monitors price breakouts from these zones and flags reclaim signals when price returns to the Value Area with confirmation from engulfing candlestick patterns and volume momentum, suggesting that a preceding breakout move may be exhausting or failing.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Value Migration
indicators.description: Builds a value area for every completed session (daily anchor, 25 rows, 70% by default) and classifies it against the prior one under the overlapping value rules: higher, lower, overlapping, unchanged or outside. Boxes, POC lines and labels mark each session, a dashboard tracks the developing area, streak and sequence, and eight alerts cover categories, streaks and extremes without acceptance.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Variable Sine Wave Fit
indicators.description: The Variable Sine Wave Fit applies least-squares regression to recent price, fitting a sine wave with damped, expanding, or constant amplitude on top of a linear trend, then projects the curve forward with RMSE error bands and marked turning points. A dashboard classifies the regime and reports the dominant cycle length for cycle-minded traders.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Vertical Horizontal Filter
indicators.description: Plots the Vertical Horizontal Filter (the spread of the window's closes divided by total close-to-close travel over 28 bars) and reads it against its own history via a 28-period SMA basis or a percentile, since the ratio has no universal threshold. Line and fill color by regime, a label names the current state, and four alerts cover basis crosses and slope turns.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: VIDYA
indicators.description: VIDYA plots Tushar Chande's Variable Index Dynamic Average, an EMA whose speed is rescaled every bar: by absolute CMO momentum (default, length 12, scaler lookback 9) or by Chande's original standard-deviation ratio. An ATR-normalized slope test colors trending and flat regimes, and a dashboard shows the live effective length. For trend traders who want one average for fast and slow tape.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Visible Range Mean Deviation Histogram
indicators.description: The Visible Range Mean Deviation Histogram maps the prices on your visible chart into bins anchored at their mean and sized by standard deviation, counting observations relative to highs and lows for an unusually smooth profile. Points of Control mark the most populated bins as candidate support and resistance for range and mean-reversion traders.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volatility Cones
indicators.description: Draws volatility cones from rolling realized volatility at five horizons, 20 to 120 bars by default: min, percentile bands, median and max from a 504-observation sample, with each horizon's current reading marked inside the cone. Manually entered implied volatilities can be overlaid per horizon, a dashboard reports ranks and positions, and four alerts flag rich, depressed and record readings.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volatility Contraction Pattern
indicators.description: Volatility Contraction Pattern detects Mark Minervini's tightening base: two to four successively shallower pullbacks (depth ratio 0.75), a qualified uptrend, and volume drying into the final coil. It draws the zigzag with depth labels, the pivot line, the stop under the last contraction, and marks breakouts on 1.5x volume expansion. For swing traders who trade bases, not predictions.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volatility Estimators
indicators.description: Volatility Estimators computes a chosen statistical volatility estimate over a lookback window and plots it as a single line, with a method selector covering Close-to-Close (default), Zero-Trend, Parkinson, Garman-Klass, and Rogers-Satchell. The range-based methods use intrabar high, low, open, and close data rather than closes alone. Defaults are a length of 10 with an annualize toggle; each estimator is implemented in its standard published form.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volatility of Volatility
indicators.description: Volatility of Volatility measures how unstable a volatility series itself is: a 20-bar standard deviation of changes in realized volatility, ATR, or an implied index, percentile-ranked over 252 bars. Readings above the 80th percentile flag regimes where ATR stops and volatility-sized positions go stale fastest. For traders whose risk numbers depend on volatility staying put.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volatility Ratio
indicators.description: Volatility Ratio plots a dimensionless activity gauge in two constructions: Schwager's wide-range-bar test (true range against a 14-bar baseline, with event diamonds above 2) or short 5-bar volatility over a long 20-bar baseline, read around 1. A dashboard adds the close-in-range directional hint. For traders who want unusual bars flagged the moment they print.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volatility Regime Switches
indicators.description: Classifies volatility into Quiet, Normal, and Stressed states from ATR, realized volatility, or Bollinger Band width, normalized as a ratio to average or a percentile rank. A hysteresis-buffered state machine with 2-bar confirmation commits each switch, drawn with threshold zones, switch markers, and a playbook dashboard for traders who adapt parameters to conditions.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volatility Signature Plot
indicators.description: Plots realized volatility against sampling interval (six configurable points from 1 to 60 minutes, averaged over 20 completed days) as a curve beside price, diagnosing microstructure bias from the fine-end slope. Upward bias flags bid-ask bounce, downward bias stale quotes; the build suggests the finest flat sampling interval and alerts when the diagnosis changes.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volatility Switch
indicators.description: Plots Ron McEwan's Volatility Switch: the standard deviation of symmetric one-bar price changes, percentile-ranked over its own trailing history so the output is confined to the 0-1 range. Readings above the 0.5 decision line mark elevated volatility that favors mean reversion, readings below it a quiet regime where trends persist, with the published 21-bar defaults for both windows.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volume Anchored Price Map
indicators.description: The Volume Anchored Price Map pairs a rolling volume profile heatmap with Z-score-validated volume bubbles, anchoring statistically extreme activity and projecting it forward as tiered liquidity levels. TIER I to III labels rank each level by deviation strength, mapping where heavy participation is most likely to make price react.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volume Bubbles & Liquidity Heatmap
indicators.description: Volume Bubbles & Liquidity Heatmap draws each higher-timeframe period's volume as a sized, color-coded bubble (total, buy/sell split, or delta) over a heatmap of traded volume per price zone. Bubbles reveal whether buyers or sellers ran each period; the heatmap shows where liquidity concentrates, putting multi-timeframe volume context on one chart.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volume by Time
indicators.description: Volume by Time averages volume by its time of day across past sessions and overlays the current session on that baseline: hollow bars for the historical norm, solid bars for today. Above-normal participation stands out the moment it prints, with average or median baselines and an optional up/down volume split for intraday traders.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volume Delta Candles
indicators.description: Volume Delta Candles builds order flow into the bars themselves, coloring a proportional segment of each candle by its intrabar volume delta estimated from lower-timeframe or live tick data. A line marks the price where the most volume traded, and delta colors that clash with the candle expose hidden buying or selling: no separate volume pane needed.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volume Delta Methods (Chart)
indicators.description: Volume Delta Methods (Chart) plots order-flow metrics straight onto the price chart: volume delta, cumulative volume delta, buy/sell volume, and total volume, rendered as lines, areas, or candlesticks. Divergences between delta polarity and price bars flag potential turns, while CVD tracks which side has controlled entire moves.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volume Delta Trailing Stop
indicators.description: The Volume Delta Trailing Stop watches for bars where lower-timeframe volume delta contradicts price direction, marks them blue or orange, and places a trigger line at their extreme. Once price breaks the trigger, a delta-governed trailing stop-line manages the position, with alerts on entries and stop breaks: order flow running both entry and exit.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volume Dry-up
indicators.description: Flags sessions whose turnover contracts to a fraction of its 50-bar average, with an optional range-contraction pair and pivot proximity filter. The lightest print of the base lookback earns the extreme dry-up (VDU) tag, and a 1.5x expansion within a 5-bar window resolves the quiet as a bullish expansion or bearish break, marked on both the volume pane and the price chart.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volume Flow Indicator
indicators.description: Builds Markos Katsanos' Volume Flow Indicator to its published specification: volume signed by the direction of typical-price changes, filtered through a volatility-scaled noise cutoff, capped at 2.5x average, and summed over 130 bars into a zero-centered oscillator. Includes the published 3-bar smoothing and an optional 5-period signal line for crossover reads.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volume Footprint
indicators.description: Volume Footprint splits every candle into equal price intervals and stacks the tick-estimated volume traded in each, turning single bars into intrabar volume profiles. Gradient or trend-colored displays show exactly where inside a candle business was done, giving lower-timeframe traders the levels that mattered within each bar.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volume Forecasting
indicators.description: Volume Forecasting projects trading volume several bars ahead by extracting the periodic rhythm in a symbol's volume history. Historical forecasts plot against realized volume, with an interquartile range framing where activity tends to settle, so traders can anticipate busy and quiet windows before they arrive.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volume Grid Heatmap
indicators.description: Volume Grid Heatmap spreads traded volume across a two-dimensional price-time grid and colors every cell by how much business it hosted. Because the time axis survives, one-off spikes separate cleanly from sustained participation: a liquidity map for traders who build entries, stops, and targets around volume structure.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volume Oscillator
indicators.description: Measures the difference between a fast and a slow moving average of volume, expressed as a percentage of the slow average, to show whether volume is expanding or contracting. Defaults are a 5-period EMA against a 10-period EMA of volume, plotted as an oscillator around zero. This is the standard raw form of the volume oscillator.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volume Profile (Maps)
indicators.description: Volume Profile (Maps) accumulates volume against every price it printed at and draws the distribution split around the latest close. The two heaviest levels are flagged in red and orange as support and resistance candidates, while empty rows expose fast-moving, low-acceptance zones. Rounding and step controls coarsen the price grid to fit any symbol.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volume Profile Matrix
indicators.description: Volume Profile Matrix slices the lookback into a grid of time columns and price rows, color-grading every cell by traded activity. Each column gets its own point of control, the busiest cell is marked in yellow, and the heaviest level projects to the latest bar: a compact view of how liquidity migrated across the window.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volume Profile Regression Channel
indicators.description: Volume Profile Regression Channel bins traded volume inside a linear regression channel fitted between two points you choose, keeping the distribution readable where trends smear horizontal profiles. A Line of Control marks the heaviest section, and a developing version tracks its migration through the window.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volume Profile with Node Detection
indicators.description: Volume Profile with Node Detection plots volume distribution across price and automatically extracts the structure inside it: peak nodes with their clusters, trough nodes, and the highest- and lowest-volume levels. Traders get ready-made acceptance and rejection zones instead of a raw histogram to eyeball.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volume Signature per Pattern
indicators.description: Detects consolidations whose 14-bar span compresses to within 2x the 200-bar ATR, then audits the classical volume signature: contraction while the pattern forms and expansion of at least 1.5x recent average at the break. Every resolved breakout is tagged Confirmed or Suspect, with zone boxes, a live formation-volume read, and a dashboard verdict.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volume Surprise
indicators.description: Volume Surprise scores how far each bar's volume deviates from the level history says is typical for that exact time, plotting actual against expected and projecting the expected path forward. A deviation histogram exposes unusually heavy or quiet participation around news, earnings, and session rhythms.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volume Zone Oscillator
indicators.description: Implements Khalil and Steckler's Volume Zone Oscillator: a 14-period EMA of close-signed volume divided by an EMA of total volume, bounded between -100 and +100. The published zone framework is drawn in the pane (regime boundaries at +5 and -5, overbought and oversold at 40 and -40, extremes at 60 and -60), with eight alerts covering regime starts, zone entries, and fades.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volume Zones Internal Visualizer
indicators.description: Volume Zones Internal Visualizer rebuilds every chart candle from lower-timeframe data, boxing its range and shading where volume concentrated inside it. The busiest intrabar close becomes a Peak Activity Level that extends forward until crossed: per-candle volume structure at a glance.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volume-adjusted MA
indicators.description: Implements Richard Arms' volume-adjusted moving average: price is weighted in fixed increments of typical volume, so the window stretches over thin tape and compresses when activity surges. Runs a 20-increment budget with Arms' 0.67 factor by default, plus slope coloring, an optional comparison SMA, and a dashboard reporting the elastic lookback and budget fill.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volume-adjusted Time
indicators.description: Re-samples price onto a volume clock: a candle prints once a volume threshold fills (average daily volume divided by 12 target bars by default), so chart space measures participation rather than minutes. The strip renders at equal widths or stretched across true elapsed time, a dashboard reports threshold, progress and pace, and three alerts cover every printed bar.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volume-weighted MACD
indicators.description: Rebuilds MACD on volume-weighted averages: a 12-period fast VWMA minus a 26-period slow VWMA with a 9-period signal line, so heavily traded bars drive the momentum read while quiet drift barely moves it. An optional classic price-only MACD overlay exposes where participation disagrees with price, alongside a histogram shaded by momentum expansion.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volumetric Order Flow Structure
indicators.description: Volumetric Order Flow Structure verifies market-structure breaks with the volume behind them: BOS and CHoCH events plot with bars scaled by the breakout candle's delta, order blocks carry stepped 15-row volume profiles with an orange point of control, and manipulation bubbles flag wicks that raid liquidity without closing through.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volumetric Regression Heatmap
indicators.description: Volumetric Regression Heatmap surrounds a volatility-adaptive regression fit with volume-weighted heat bands, showing where activity concentrated relative to the trend. Mean-reversion signals fire at the deviation bands when volatility contracts, delta histograms track aggressive pressure, and the fit projects forward.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Volumetric Toolkit
indicators.description: Volumetric Toolkit packs four volume-driven price action reads into one indicator: Ranges of Interest around high-liquidity candles, Impulses where volume and price break out together, Levels of Interest at heavily traded closes, and volume divergences that catch trends losing participation. Volume evidence behind every level you draw.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Vortex Indicator
indicators.description: The Vortex Indicator sums upward and downward vortex movements (the distances between the current high or low and the prior low or high) and divides each by the sum of true range over the window, yielding the VI+ and VI- lines whose crossings track directional movement. It uses the classic default length of 14. This is a straight implementation of the standard calculation.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: VSA Test Bar
indicators.description: Marks the VSA test: a narrow, low-volume probe into a recent high-volume supply area that closes firm and holds. Test volume must stay below 0.7x the 20-bar average and half the supply volume by default, with confirmation from an up bar on rising volume within 5 bars. Supply areas, an invalidation line at the test low, failed-test flags and four alerts complete the read.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: VWAP
indicators.description: Computes the volume-weighted average price of a session, summing price times volume and dividing by cumulative volume from the anchor point, then resetting at each new period. The anchor defaults to the trading day, with week and month options, and bands can be toggled at plus or minus 1, 2, and 3 standard deviations or fixed percentages around the VWAP line. This is the standard raw implementation of session VWAP with no modifications.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: VWAP Bands - Event Based
indicators.description: VWAP Bands - Event Based plots standard-deviation bands around a VWAP that restarts on the event you pick: periodically, on new higher highs or lower lows, on trend changes, at an anchor, or on an external cross. The reset governs the line's smoothness, making it a flexible trailing support/resistance or a source for other tools.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: VWAP Mean-reversion vs Trend Regimes
indicators.description: Classifies each intraday session as trending or mean-reverting from four VWAP tells (crossings, side hold, slope, and stretch), scored into a 0-100 composite over a 48-bar evidence window. Session VWAP and its first and outer deviation bands recolor by regime, setup alerts fire for outer-band fades and pullback joins, and a dashboard states the active playbook.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: VWAP Periodic Close
indicators.description: Plots the level where VWAP finished each period (daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly and yearly) as labeled horizontal references that stay on the chart. Every timeframe toggles independently and several historical closes can be kept visible at once, giving traders a clean map of where volume-weighted value settled, period after period.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: VWAP Pinch
indicators.description: Tracks two anchored VWAPs (one from the latest confirmed swing high, one from the swing low) and flags a pinch when they converge within 1 ATR with price closing between them. Acceptance beyond either line on 2 consecutive closes resolves the coil, fades the abandoned anchor, and hands the surviving VWAP over as the working support or resistance.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Waddah Attar Explosion
indicators.description: The definitive clean build of the Waddah Attar Explosion: trend power columns from the sensitivity-scaled change of a 20/40 EMA MACD line, read against an explosion line set by the 20-period, 2-deviation Bollinger Band width and a configurable dead zone floor. Columns stay dimmed until directional energy clears both gates, reserving full color for tradeable expansion.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Wave Consolidation
indicators.description: Builds consolidation zones from the market's own swings: each move that sets a higher-high or lower-low gets a volume profile, and a zone grows outward from its point of control. Overlapping zones merge to keep charts readable, and mitigated zones collapse to dotted outlines: volume-backed support and resistance for range and reversal traders.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Wave Degree Hierarchy
indicators.description: Builds up to four nested Elliott degrees from one 8-bar base zigzag, deriving each higher degree recursively from the pivots below and labeling swings in each degree's own notation. Proportion checks flag corrections too small or too large for their degree, a dashboard tracks per-degree legs, corrections and invalidation levels, and eleven alerts cover the structure.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Wave Extension
indicators.description: Detects completed five-wave impulses from 10-bar swings and labels the extended wave once its length reaches 1.618x the next largest motive wave and it subdivides into its own five sub-waves. While a third wave extends, wave 5 targets print at equality with wave 1 and 0.618 of waves 0-3; near-equal waves 1 and 3 raise an extended-fifth watch, with eight alerts in total.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Wave Trend Oscillator
indicators.description: Plots the WT1 wave and its WT2 signal line in a dedicated pane: smoothed, deviation-scaled momentum swinging around zero with paired overbought/oversold levels at 53/60 and -53/-60. Defaults follow the widely used construction (HLC3 source, channel length 10, average length 21, signal length 4), for traders timing reversals at momentum extremes.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Wavelet Decomposition
indicators.description: Runs a shift-invariant wavelet pyramid over a rolling 256-bar window, splitting the source into stacked detail lanes (D1 holding 2-4 bar moves, each level an octave slower) plus a trend approximation, all summing back to the source exactly. Denoised and trend reconstructions draw over price, the revising right edge is shaded, and an energy table ranks the timescales.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Weekly Stacked Daily Changes
indicators.description: Stacks every week's daily net price changes into a single column, so each weekday's contribution and the week's total volatility sit side by side. It renders with zero configuration, while width, spacing, colors and month markers stay adjustable, and the Bottom Stack Bias option anchors stacks to weekly net return, separating up-weeks from down-weeks at a glance.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Whittaker Envelope
indicators.description: Fits a smooth, adaptive envelope to price using Whittaker–Eilers smoothing with asymmetric least squares: the upper band bends toward peaks, the lower toward troughs, and a midline tracks the structural path between them. Band width maps volatility expansion and compression, with optional slope extrapolation. A repainting research tool for structure, not live signals.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Wide-range Bar
indicators.description: Detects bars that traveled far beyond their recent context: by default the widest span in a 7-bar window, or 1.5x a 14-bar average range or ATR baseline. Qualifying bars are colored by where they close within their span, tagged with WRB labels reporting the exact expansion ratio, and covered by four alerts, with an optional volume filter and midpoint level.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Williams %R
indicators.description: Williams %R plots the position of the current close relative to the highest high and lowest low of a lookback window, on an inverted scale from 0 to -100 where readings near 0 indicate closes at the top of the range. The default length is 14. This is the standard implementation of Larry Williams' %R with the classic setting.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Williams A/D
indicators.description: Plots Larry Williams' cumulative accumulation/distribution line in its original price-only form: each bar adds the close's progress from the true low on up-closes and subtracts its distance from the true high on down-closes, with an optional volume-weighted variant. A 20-period EMA smoothing, directional coloring and automatic divergence detection complete the build.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Williams Alligator
indicators.description: Plots three smoothed moving averages of median price, the Jaw, Teeth, and Lips, each shifted forward in time, so their spread and order indicate trending versus ranging conditions. Defaults are SMMA lengths of 13, 8, and 5 with forward offsets of 8, 5, and 3 bars respectively. This is the standard implementation of Bill Williams' Alligator.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Williams Fractal
indicators.description: Marks fractal points on the chart, an up fractal at a high flanked by lower highs on both sides and a down fractal at a low flanked by higher lows, confirmed only after the flanking bars have printed. The default period of 2 requires two bars on each side of the extreme, matching Bill Williams' original definition. This is the plain, standard Williams Fractal implementation.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Windowed FIR Smoothing
indicators.description: Smooths price with a windowed FIR average, Hann weights by default, with Hamming, Triangular and Rectangular (SMA) profiles, over a 21-bar lookback, colored by slope on the chart. An optional 50-bar second average forms a fast/slow pair with a difference fill and cross alerts, and a dashboard reports each window's exact (N - 1) / 2 bar delay.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Wolfe Wave Detector
indicators.description: Finds five-point Wolfe Wave patterns automatically by scanning multiple swing lengths at once, drawing the XABCD structure and projecting the target line where a reversal is anticipated. Symmetry controls filter out poorly formed channels, dots mark every target hit, and a dashboard tallies patterns detected against targets reached.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Woodie Pivots
indicators.description: Draws the Woodie pivot ladder from a completed prior period (daily by default, weekly or monthly optional) with the close-weighted center P = (H + L + 2C) / 4 or the open-based variant, plus R1/S1 and R2/S2 tiers and an optional R3/S3. Levels hold flat until each roll, an info panel reports where the period opened versus P, and eight cross alerts cover the ladder.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Wyckoff Accumulation Schematic
indicators.description: Detects and labels the accumulation sequence on the chart (PS, SC, AR, ST, spring or higher-low test, SOS, LPS and back-up) through a state machine that demands a prior downtrend, wide spread and climactic volume. Phase zones A through D shade the range, boundaries and a markup target project forward, and a dashboard tracks the event checklist alongside nine alerts.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Wyckoff Distribution Schematic
indicators.description: Maps the distribution sequence live on the chart (PSY, BC, AR, ST, phase B upthrusts, UTAD or lower-high test, SOW and LPSY) via a state machine keyed to a prior uptrend, wide spread and climactic volume. Lettered phase zones shade the range, boundaries draw at the BC high and the ice, a markdown target projects on confirmation, and ten alerts cover the sequence.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Wyckoff Method
indicators.description: Classifies the chart into the four-stage Wyckoff campaign cycle (accumulation, markup, distribution, markdown) from stopping actions and ATR-scaled reactions, drawing range boxes, stage backgrounds and a range-height objective. A dashboard reads the three laws live (supply and demand, cause and effect, effort versus result) with a Composite Man summary and seven alerts.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Wyckoff Wave & Volume Studies
indicators.description: Segments price into alternating buying and selling waves and plots each wave's cumulative volume as columns, with zigzag legs and volume totals on the price chart. Waves complete on an ATR-scaled reversal (2 x 14-bar ATR by default) and are compared with prior waves on volume, progress and duration, tagging Opposition and Drying up reads with six alerts.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Yang-Zhang Estimator
indicators.description: Plots annualized Yang-Zhang volatility from a 20-bar OHLC window, combining the overnight-gap, open-to-close and Rogers-Satchell variance components under the variance-minimizing weight from the original 2000 paper. A 252 bars-per-year default annualizes the read; a dashed 20% threshold and an optional 60-bar comparison window drive four alerts, with components plottable separately.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Zero-lag MACD
indicators.description: The familiar MACD run on de-lagged averages: each EMA is error-corrected by doubling it and subtracting the EMA of that EMA, so crosses at the signal line and zero line arrive a few bars ahead of the classic study. Standard 12/26/9 defaults, a switchable de-lagged signal line, a histogram shaded by whether the spread is widening, a zero-line gradient fill and six alerts.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: Zig Zag Channels
indicators.description: Connects rolling-window peaks and troughs into a zigzag, then adds upper and lower extremities that wrap the swings in a channel. Pivots give clean anchor points for Fibonacci and other drawing tools, while the extended extremities mark potential support and resistance. Components backpaint, keeping every leg honest about when it was confirmed.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: ZigZag
indicators.description: Connects successive swing highs and swing lows with straight line segments, filtering out price movements smaller than a set threshold to show the larger swings in price. Defaults are a 5 percent deviation filter with a pivot depth of 10 bars, and the most recent leg repaints until a new pivot is confirmed. This is the standard raw ZigZag construction.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

indicators.name: ZLEMA
indicators.description: A 21-period zero-lag EMA that smooths a de-lagged input, the current price doubled, minus the price (N - 1) / 2 bars back, so the line hugs trends and turns earlier than an equal-length EMA. Ships with slope coloring, a price/ZLEMA gradient fill, an optional slower second ZLEMA crossover pair, a same-length EMA benchmark, a dashboard and six alerts.
indicators.author: LuxAlgo

concepts.name: Adaptive-lookback MA
concepts.blurb: An adaptive-lookback MA (often just "adaptive moving average") is a moving average whose effective length is recomputed on every bar rather than fixed in advance.

concepts.name: ADX / DMI System
concepts.blurb: The ADX / DMI System is J. Welles Wilder's directional movement framework, published in his 1978 book New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems.

concepts.name: Alligator
concepts.blurb: The Alligator is Bill Williams' three-line trend tool from the mid-1990s.

concepts.name: ALMA
concepts.blurb: ALMA (the Arnaud Legoux Moving Average) is a windowed weighted average introduced by Arnaud Legoux and Dimitrios Kouzis-Loukas in 2009.

concepts.name: Anchored MA
concepts.blurb: An anchored moving average starts at a chosen event and averages every bar from that point forward, so its window expands instead of sliding.

concepts.name: Andrews' Pitchfork
concepts.blurb: Andrews' Pitchfork is a three-point channel tool built around a median line.

concepts.name: Aroon
concepts.blurb: Aroon is a pair of lines Tushar Chande introduced in 1995 that measure time instead of magnitude.

concepts.name: ATR Trailing Regime
concepts.blurb: An ATR Trailing Regime is a trend-following construct in which a stop line is offset from price by a multiple of the ATR and ratchets in the trend's favor.

concepts.name: Bessel Filter
concepts.blurb: A Bessel filter is a low-pass filter design whose defining property is maximally flat group delay: every frequency component that passes through it is delayed by very nearly the same number of bars.

concepts.name: Breakout
concepts.blurb: A breakout is a move that closes beyond a boundary the market had been respecting: a range extreme, a support or resistance level, a pattern border, a channel line, or a prior session high or low.

concepts.name: Butterworth Filter
concepts.blurb: A Butterworth filter is a low-pass filter design whose magnitude response is maximally flat in the passband: the wavelengths it keeps are passed with as little amplitude distortion as mathematically…

concepts.name: Chande Kroll Stop
concepts.blurb: The Chande Kroll stop is a volatility-based trailing stop that plots two lines on the chart: a stop for long positions below price and a stop for short positions above it.

concepts.name: Chandelier Stop
concepts.blurb: The chandelier stop, usually called the chandelier exit, is a volatility-scaled trailing stop developed by Chuck LeBeau and popularized by Alexander Elder.

concepts.name: Chebyshev Filters
concepts.blurb: Chebyshev filters are recursive low-pass filters borrowed from classical signal processing, named after mathematician Pafnuty Chebyshev, whose polynomials shape their frequency response.

concepts.name: Climactic Moves
concepts.blurb: Climactic moves are the terminal accelerations of a trend: price steepens into a near-vertical run on expanding ranges and unusually heavy volume.

concepts.name: Continuation
concepts.blurb: Continuation is the resolution of a pause in the direction of the prevailing trend: an impulse leg runs, price digests through a pullback, flag, or range, and the next leg then breaks out the same…

concepts.name: Coral Trend
concepts.blurb: The Coral Trend is a heavily smoothed trend line from the moving-average lineage, built by cascading several stages of exponential smoothing (common implementations chain six) and recombining the…

concepts.name: Correlation Trend Indicator
concepts.blurb: The Correlation Trend Indicator (CTI) is John Ehlers' answer to a deceptively simple question: how much does recent price look like a straight line?

concepts.name: Death Cross
concepts.blurb: A death cross is the bearish counterpart of the golden cross: a shorter moving average crossing below a longer one, classically the 50-day simple moving average dropping under the 200-day on a daily…

concepts.name: DEMA
concepts.blurb: DEMA, the double exponential moving average, is a lag-reduced average rather than an average applied twice.

concepts.name: Displaced MA
concepts.blurb: A displaced moving average is an ordinary moving average shifted horizontally by a fixed number of bars.

concepts.name: Donchian Trend Rules
concepts.blurb: Donchian Trend Rules are the mechanical trend-following rules built on channel breakouts: go long when price makes a new N-period high, and exit or reverse when it makes a new M-period low (mirrored…

concepts.name: Dynamic S/R Via MA
concepts.blurb: Dynamic S/R via MA treats a moving average as support or resistance that moves with price instead of sitting at a fixed level.

concepts.name: Ehlers Instantaneous Trendline
concepts.blurb: The Ehlers Instantaneous Trendline is a low-lag smoother introduced by John Ehlers, built on the idea that price can be modeled as trend plus cycle.

concepts.name: Ehlers SuperSmoother
concepts.blurb: The SuperSmoother is a two-pole low-pass filter John Ehlers adapted from Butterworth filter design for market data.

concepts.name: Elastic Volume-weighted MA
concepts.blurb: The elastic volume-weighted moving average (eVWMA), introduced by Christian Fries, is a recursive average in which volume sets each bar's influence.

concepts.name: Elliptic Filter
concepts.blurb: An elliptic filter, also called a Cauer filter after the German engineer Wilhelm Cauer, is the most aggressive of the classical low-pass designs: for a given filter order it achieves the fastest…

concepts.name: EMA
concepts.blurb: An EMA (exponential moving average) is a weighted average of price in which the weights decay exponentially with age: the newest bar counts most, and each older bar counts a fixed fraction less.

concepts.name: Fan Principle
concepts.blurb: The fan principle is a classical charting technique in which successive trendlines are drawn from the same anchor point as a trend decelerates.

concepts.name: FRAMA
concepts.blurb: FRAMA, the fractal adaptive moving average, is John Ehlers' adaptive smoother: an EMA whose smoothing factor is recomputed every bar from the estimated fractal dimension of recent price.

concepts.name: Gann Box
concepts.blurb: A Gann Box is a rectangular chart overlay anchored between two significant points, usually a major swing low and swing high, that subdivides the move in both price and time.

concepts.name: Gann Fan & Angles
concepts.blurb: Gann angles are lines drawn from a significant pivot at fixed rates of price change per unit of time, and a Gann Fan projects the standard set of them from one anchor.

concepts.name: Gann HiLo Activator
concepts.blurb: The Gann HiLo Activator is a trailing trend line built from two simple moving averages: one of the highs and one of the lows, each over a short lookback (3 periods is the common default).

concepts.name: Gann Square of 9
concepts.blurb: The Gann Square of 9 is W.D. Gann's number spiral: integers wind outward from 1 at the center, and numbers falling on the same angle of the spiral are treated as harmonically related prices.

concepts.name: Gaussian Filter
concepts.blurb: A Gaussian filter smooths price with a weighting that follows the Gaussian bell curve, the shape of the normal distribution named for Carl Friedrich Gauss.

concepts.name: Geometric MA
concepts.blurb: A geometric MA replaces the arithmetic mean inside a simple moving average with the geometric mean: multiply the last N prices together and take the Nth root.

concepts.name: Golden Cross
concepts.blurb: A golden cross is the event where a shorter moving average crosses above a longer one, and in its classic form specifically the 50-day simple moving average crossing above the 200-day on a daily…

concepts.name: Guppy GMMA
concepts.blurb: The Guppy Multiple Moving Average, developed by Australian trader Daryl Guppy, plots two groups of six EMAs: a short-term group (traditionally 3, 5, 8, 10, 12 and 15 periods) standing in for traders,…

concepts.name: Halftrend
concepts.blurb: Halftrend is a trailing trend line known for going flat when the market pauses.

concepts.name: Harmonic MA
concepts.blurb: A harmonic MA smooths price with the harmonic mean instead of the arithmetic mean: over an n-bar window it equals n divided by the sum of the reciprocals of the prices.

concepts.name: Higher-timeframe Trend Filter
concepts.blurb: A higher-timeframe trend filter is a permission rule: signals generated on the timeframe you trade are taken only when they agree with the trend one or more steps above.

concepts.name: HMA
concepts.blurb: The HMA (Hull Moving Average) is a low-lag moving average published by Alan Hull in 2005.

concepts.name: Ichimoku Signals
concepts.blurb: Ichimoku Signals are the named events traders take from the Ichimoku System's five lines.

concepts.name: Ichimoku System
concepts.blurb: The Ichimoku System (Ichimoku Kinko Hyo, roughly 'one-glance equilibrium chart') is a complete charting method developed by the Japanese journalist Goichi Hosoda and published in 1969 after decades…

concepts.name: Ichimoku Theories
concepts.blurb: The Ichimoku Theories are the three doctrines Goichi Hosoda (who wrote as Ichimoku Sanjin) built beneath the five-line chart: time theory, wave theory, and price observation theory.

concepts.name: JMA
concepts.blurb: JMA (the Jurik Moving Average) is an adaptive moving average developed by Mark Jurik of Jurik Research.

concepts.name: KAMA
concepts.blurb: KAMA, Perry Kaufman's adaptive moving average, is an exponential average whose smoothing constant changes bar by bar with how efficiently price is moving.

concepts.name: Kaufman Efficiency Ratio
concepts.blurb: The Kaufman Efficiency Ratio measures how directly price traveled over a lookback window.

concepts.name: Laguerre Filter
concepts.blurb: The Laguerre filter is a smoother John Ehlers built from the Laguerre transform, a mathematical basis that lets a filter spend its memory unevenly across time.

concepts.name: Linear-regression Channel
concepts.blurb: A linear-regression channel fits a straight line to price over a fixed lookback using ordinary least squares, the same fit described under linear regression: the line that minimizes the sum of…

concepts.name: LSMA
concepts.blurb: LSMA, the least-squares moving average, fits a straight line to the last N closes by ordinary least squares (linear regression) and plots the value of that line at the current bar.

concepts.name: MA Envelope
concepts.blurb: An MA Envelope is a moving average with two bands offset above and below it by a fixed amount, most often a set percentage of the average's value (hence the alias "percent bands").

concepts.name: MAMA/FAMA
concepts.blurb: MAMA is John Ehlers' MESA Adaptive Moving Average, published in 2001; FAMA, the Following Adaptive Moving Average, is its companion line.

concepts.name: MA of MA
concepts.blurb: An MA of MA is double smoothing: a moving average computed not on price but on the output of another moving average.

concepts.name: MA Ribbon
concepts.blurb: An MA ribbon (or MA fan) plots one moving average many times at stepped lengths, for example eight EMAs from 20 to 55, and reads them as a single band.

concepts.name: MA Slope Filter
concepts.blurb: An MA slope filter uses the direction of a moving average itself, rather than price's position relative to it, as the trend condition.

concepts.name: McGinley Dynamic
concepts.blurb: The McGinley Dynamic is an adaptive smoothing line developed by market technician John R. McGinley in the 1990s to address a standing complaint about moving averages: a fixed length is always tuned…

concepts.name: MLMA
concepts.blurb: MLMA stands for Machine Learning Moving Average: a smoothing line whose value comes from fitting a statistical learning model to recent prices instead of applying a fixed weighting scheme.

concepts.name: Moving Average Crossovers
concepts.blurb: Moving average crossovers are the events where one plotted average crosses another, or where price crosses an average.

concepts.name: NRTR
concepts.blurb: NRTR (Nick Rypock Trailing Reverse) is a trailing stop-and-reverse line developed by Konstantin Kopyrkin and published in 2001.

concepts.name: Order-statistic Filters
concepts.blurb: Order-statistic filters smooth a series by ranking rather than averaging.

concepts.name: Parabolic SAR
concepts.blurb: The Parabolic SAR (stop and reverse) is a trailing stop system introduced by J. Welles Wilder in his 1978 book New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems.

concepts.name: Parallel Channel
concepts.blurb: A parallel channel (or equidistant channel) is two same-slope lines containing a trend: a trendline drawn along the swing lows and a parallel copy along the swing highs for a rising channel, the…

concepts.name: Polynomial Regression Band
concepts.blurb: A polynomial regression band is a curved channel built by fitting a polynomial to recent prices with least squares, then offsetting the fitted curve above and below by a volatility measure, usually a…

concepts.name: Pullback
concepts.blurb: A pullback is a counter-trend move inside an intact trend: price gives back part of the most recent advance (or decline), then the trend resumes.

concepts.name: Rainbow MA Stack
concepts.blurb: A rainbow MA stack plots many moving averages at once, colored in a gradient so the group reads as a single band.

concepts.name: Random Walk Index
concepts.blurb: The Random Walk Index (RWI) asks a blunt statistical question of every price move: did price travel further than a random walk would have?

concepts.name: Retest
concepts.blurb: A retest is a return to a level that price has already broken, approached now from the other side.

concepts.name: Reversal
concepts.blurb: A reversal is a durable change in the direction of the prevailing trend: an uptrend rolling over into a downtrend, or a downtrend turning up.

concepts.name: RMA
concepts.blurb: The RMA (running moving average) is the recursive smoother J. Welles Wilder introduced in his 1978 book New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems, which is why it also goes by Wilder smoothing or the…

concepts.name: R-squared Trend Fit
concepts.blurb: An R-squared trend fit measures trend strength by running a linear regression of price against time over a lookback window and reporting R-squared, the fraction of price variance explained by the…

concepts.name: Sine-weighted MA
concepts.blurb: A sine-weighted MA (SWMA) is a windowed FIR moving average whose weights trace half a sine cycle across the lookback window.

concepts.name: SMA
concepts.blurb: A simple moving average (SMA) is the arithmetic mean of the last N values of a series, usually closing prices, recomputed on every bar.

concepts.name: Speed Resistance Lines
concepts.blurb: Speed resistance lines, or speedlines, are a fan tool credited to market analyst Edson Gould.

concepts.name: Standard-error Channel
concepts.blurb: A standard-error channel is a linear regression line drawn through a lookback window with parallel bands offset above and below by a multiple of the standard error of estimate, the statistic…

concepts.name: Supertrend
concepts.blurb: Supertrend is a volatility-trailing overlay that plots a single stop-and-reverse line: below price while the trend state is up, above it while the state is down.

concepts.name: Swiss Army Knife Filter
concepts.blurb: The Swiss Army Knife filter is John Ehlers' name for a single generalized second-order recursive filter that becomes many different indicators depending only on which coefficient set is plugged in.

concepts.name: SWMA
concepts.blurb: The SWMA, or symmetric weighted moving average, is a moving average whose weights are mirrored around the center of its window.

concepts.name: T3
concepts.blurb: T3 is a smoothing technique introduced by Tim Tillson in "Smoothing Techniques For More Accurate Signals" (Technical Analysis of Stocks & Commodities, January 1998).

concepts.name: TEMA
concepts.blurb: TEMA (triple exponential moving average) is a reduced-lag smoother introduced by Patrick Mulloy in 1994, alongside its sibling DEMA.

concepts.name: TRAMA
concepts.blurb: TRAMA, the Trend Regularity Adaptive Moving Average, is an adaptive average introduced by LuxAlgo whose smoothing factor is driven by how regularly price prints new extremes.

concepts.name: Trend Acceleration/inflection
concepts.blurb: Trend acceleration/inflection is the study of a trend's second derivative: not whether price is rising, but whether the rise is speeding up, slowing down, or bending over.

concepts.name: Trend Exhaustion
concepts.blurb: Trend exhaustion is the condition late in a directional move when the buying or selling that drove it stops being replenished: price is still trending, but each push covers less ground, momentum…

concepts.name: Trend Intensity Index
concepts.blurb: The Trend Intensity Index (TII) measures how one-sided price has been relative to its own moving average.

concepts.name: Trendline
concepts.blurb: A trendline is a straight line drawn across successive swing points and projected forward: under rising lows to mark diagonal support in an uptrend, over falling highs to mark diagonal resistance in…

concepts.name: Trend Magic
concepts.blurb: Trend Magic is a trailing trend line that takes its direction from momentum rather than from price alone.

concepts.name: Trend-quality Composites
concepts.blurb: Trend-quality composites are indicators that reduce several trend measurements (direction, strength, smoothness, volatility context) into a single score of how clean and tradeable the current trend…

concepts.name: Trend Regime Label
concepts.blurb: A trend regime label is a discrete classification stamped on each bar: uptrend, downtrend, or range, sometimes with strength grades.

concepts.name: Triangular MA
concepts.blurb: A triangular moving average is a simple moving average smoothed a second time: an SMA of an SMA, with each pass covering roughly half the stated period (platforms differ on how odd lengths are split,…

concepts.name: UHL Adaptive MA
concepts.blurb: The UHL Adaptive MA, credited to Andreas Uhl and often published as the corrected moving average (CMA), is an average that updates only when movement is statistically meaningful.

concepts.name: Ultimate Smoother
concepts.blurb: The Ultimate Smoother is a low-pass price filter introduced by John Ehlers in 2024, designed around a blunt objective: zero lag in the passband.

concepts.name: Vertical Horizontal Filter
concepts.blurb: The Vertical Horizontal Filter (VHF) is a trend-versus-range gauge built on a simple geometric idea: in a trend, price movement is mostly vertical (net progress), while in a range it is mostly…

concepts.name: VIDYA
concepts.blurb: VIDYA (Variable Index Dynamic Average) is Tushar Chande's adaptive moving average: an EMA whose smoothing constant is rescaled every bar by how decisively price is moving.

concepts.name: Volume-adjusted MA
concepts.blurb: A volume-adjusted moving average weights each bar's price by how much trading it carried, so heavily traded bars pull the average toward their price and quiet bars barely register.

concepts.name: Vortex
concepts.blurb: The Vortex Indicator (VI) is a two-line trend tool published by Etienne Botes and Douglas Siepman in 2010, named for an analogy to vortex flows observed in nature.

concepts.name: VWMA
concepts.blurb: A VWMA (volume-weighted moving average) is a rolling average in which each bar's price is weighted by that bar's volume: over the last N bars, the sum of price times volume divided by the sum of…

concepts.name: Whittaker–Henderson Smoother
concepts.blurb: The Whittaker–Henderson smoother is a penalized least-squares method, proposed by Whittaker in 1923 and developed in actuarial graduation work by Henderson, that balances two competing costs:…

concepts.name: Windowed FIR Smoothing
concepts.blurb: Windowed FIR smoothing is moving-average construction using the window functions of signal processing.

concepts.name: WMA
concepts.blurb: A WMA (weighted moving average) is a moving average that assigns linearly increasing weights to more recent bars.

concepts.name: ZLEMA
concepts.blurb: A ZLEMA (zero-lag exponential moving average) is an EMA applied to a de-lagged version of price rather than to price itself.

concepts.name: 5/35 Oscillator
concepts.blurb: The 5/35 Oscillator, widely known as the Elliott Wave Oscillator (EWO), is the difference between a 5-period and a 35-period simple moving average, plotted as a histogram around zero.

concepts.name: Accelerator Oscillator
concepts.blurb: The Accelerator Oscillator (AC) is Bill Williams' measure of momentum's acceleration.

concepts.name: Accumulative Swing Index
concepts.blurb: The Accumulative Swing Index (ASI), also written as the accumulation swing index and abbreviated ASI, is a running total of J. Welles Wilder's Swing Index, published in his 1978 book New Concepts in…

concepts.name: Adaptive/dynamic RSI
concepts.blurb: Wilder's RSI runs on three fixed choices: the conventional 14-bar lookback, his own smoothing, and static 70/30 thresholds.

concepts.name: Adaptive Stochastic
concepts.blurb: An Adaptive Stochastic is a Stochastic Oscillator whose lookback is not fixed but recomputed bar by bar from a measurement of current conditions, most commonly the dominant cycle period.

concepts.name: APO
concepts.blurb: APO, the Absolute Price Oscillator, is the difference between a fast and a slow moving average of price, plotted around zero and denominated in price units (dollars, points, pips).

concepts.name: Awesome Oscillator
concepts.blurb: The Awesome Oscillator (AO) is Bill Williams' momentum histogram: a 5-period simple moving average of the bar midpoint (high plus low, halved) minus a 34-period SMA of the same midpoint.

concepts.name: Balance of Power
concepts.blurb: Balance of Power (BOP) is a bar-anatomy oscillator that scores who won each candle.

concepts.name: Cardwell Positive/negative Reversals
concepts.blurb: Positive and negative reversals are RSI patterns described by Andrew Cardwell, an analyst known for reinterpreting RSI as a trend tool rather than a reversal tool.

concepts.name: CCI
concepts.blurb: CCI, the Commodity Channel Index, was introduced by Donald Lambert in 1980 to measure how far price has strayed from its own average.

concepts.name: Centerline Regime
concepts.blurb: A centerline regime is a read of which side of its midline an oscillator occupies: above the centerline is treated as a bullish regime, below as bearish, independent of any overbought or oversold…

concepts.name: Center of Gravity
concepts.blurb: The Center of Gravity is John Ehlers's oscillator, published in 2002, that locates the balance point of recent prices.

concepts.name: Chande Forecast Oscillator
concepts.blurb: The Chande Forecast Oscillator (CFO) measures how far price sits from where a linear regression says it should be.

concepts.name: Chande Momentum Oscillator
concepts.blurb: The Chande Momentum Oscillator (CMO) is a bounded momentum oscillator introduced by Tushar Chande.

concepts.name: Connors RSI
concepts.blurb: Connors RSI is a composite oscillator published by Larry Connors' research group for short-term mean reversion.

concepts.name: Constance Brown Studies
concepts.blurb: The Constance Brown Studies are a family of RSI-derived momentum tools from Constance Brown's Technical Analysis for the Trading Professional (1999), each built to repair a specific weakness of RSI…

concepts.name: Coppock Curve
concepts.blurb: The Coppock Curve is a long-horizon momentum gauge built from smoothed rate of change.

concepts.name: Cyber Cycle
concepts.blurb: The Cyber Cycle is John Ehlers' filter for extracting the cyclical component of price.

concepts.name: Detrended Price Oscillator
concepts.blurb: The Detrended Price Oscillator (DPO) removes the longer trend from price so that shorter cycles stand out.

concepts.name: Disparity Index
concepts.blurb: The Disparity Index measures how far price has stretched away from its own moving average, expressed as a percentage.

concepts.name: Divergence Variants & Confirmation
concepts.blurb: Beyond the two textbook cases, divergence comes in variants, and none of them is a trade without a confirmation rule.

concepts.name: Double Stochastic
concepts.blurb: A Double Stochastic runs the stochastic calculation twice.

concepts.name: DSS Bressert
concepts.blurb: The DSS Bressert, short for Double Smoothed Stochastic, is a momentum oscillator that applies the stochastic calculation twice with exponential smoothing in between.

concepts.name: Dynamic Momentum Index
concepts.blurb: The Dynamic Momentum Index (DMI) is a variable-length RSI: the familiar relative strength calculation whose lookback shrinks when volatility rises and stretches when volatility falls.

concepts.name: Elder Impulse System
concepts.blurb: The Elder Impulse System is a bar-coloring method from Alexander Elder that combines one trend input and one momentum input.

concepts.name: Elder Ray
concepts.blurb: Elder Ray is Alexander Elder's pair of gauges for separating buying and selling pressure around consensus value, introduced in Trading for a Living (1993).

concepts.name: Elegant Oscillator
concepts.blurb: The Elegant Oscillator is a momentum indicator by John Ehlers that combines three of his signature techniques into one bounded line: a simple price derivative, root-mean-square normalization, and the…

concepts.name: Embedded Readings
concepts.blurb: An embedded reading occurs when a bounded oscillator becomes pinned in its overbought or oversold zone and stays there bar after bar while a strong trend runs.

concepts.name: Ergodic Oscillator
concepts.blurb: The Ergodic Oscillator comes from William Blau's double-smoothing framework for momentum.

concepts.name: Firefly Oscillator
concepts.blurb: The Firefly oscillator is a momentum indicator that measures how far a weighted price sits from its own recent average, in units of recent variability, and then double-smooths that reading into a 0…

concepts.name: Fisher Transform
concepts.blurb: The Fisher Transform is John Ehlers' technique for reshaping price data into an approximately Gaussian (normal) distribution.

concepts.name: Gator Oscillator
concepts.blurb: The Gator Oscillator is Bill Williams' histogram view of his own Alligator indicator.

concepts.name: Hidden Divergence
concepts.blurb: Hidden divergence is a swing-to-swing disagreement between price and an oscillator in which the oscillator, not price, makes the more extreme print.

concepts.name: Impulse MACD
concepts.blurb: The Impulse MACD is a MACD variant engineered to go silent in ranges.

concepts.name: Intraday Momentum Index
concepts.blurb: The Intraday Momentum Index (IMI) is an RSI-style oscillator computed on candle bodies instead of close-to-close changes.

concepts.name: Inverse Fisher Transform
concepts.blurb: The Inverse Fisher Transform is John Ehlers' recipe for making an oscillator's output more decisive.

concepts.name: Know Sure Thing
concepts.blurb: The Know Sure Thing (KST) is Martin Pring's summed rate-of-change oscillator.

concepts.name: Laguerre RSI
concepts.blurb: The Laguerre RSI is John Ehlers' reworking of RSI in which the lookback window is replaced by a four-stage Laguerre filter.

concepts.name: MACD
concepts.blurb: MACD (Moving Average Convergence Divergence) is a momentum indicator built from the spread between two exponential moving averages, developed by Gerald Appel in the late 1970s.

concepts.name: MACD-V
concepts.blurb: MACD-V is a volatility-normalized MACD proposed by Alex Spiroglou in a 2022 paper.

concepts.name: Momentum
concepts.blurb: Momentum in technical analysis names two closely related things.

concepts.name: Momentum Expansion vs Contraction
concepts.blurb: Momentum expansion vs contraction is the grammar layer of oscillator reading: is the momentum reading growing or shrinking as the move develops?

concepts.name: Momentum Thrust
concepts.blurb: A momentum thrust is a fast, outsized expansion of directional momentum read as the start of a move rather than its end.

concepts.name: Oscillator of Oscillator
concepts.blurb: An oscillator of oscillator is a second-order indicator: an oscillator transformation applied to another oscillator's output rather than to price.

concepts.name: Oscillator Swing Failure
concepts.blurb: An oscillator swing failure is a reversal pattern drawn entirely on a momentum oscillator: after an extreme reading, the oscillator rallies (or dips), fails to exceed its prior extreme, and then…

concepts.name: OsMA
concepts.blurb: OsMA stands for Oscillator of a Moving Average (some platforms list it as Moving Average of Oscillator).

concepts.name: Overbought/oversold
concepts.blurb: Overbought and oversold are zone labels on bounded oscillators.

concepts.name: Polarized Fractal Efficiency
concepts.blurb: Polarized Fractal Efficiency (PFE) measures how efficiently price traveled from one point to another over a lookback window, with the sign of the reading set by the direction of the net move.

concepts.name: PPO
concepts.blurb: The PPO (percentage price oscillator) is a momentum oscillator built exactly like MACD but expressed in percentage terms.

concepts.name: Premier Stochastic
concepts.blurb: The Premier Stochastic is a smoothed, rescaled variant of the stochastic oscillator, introduced by Lee Leibfarth in a 2008 Technical Analysis of Stocks & Commodities article.

concepts.name: Pretty Good Oscillator
concepts.blurb: The Pretty Good Oscillator (PGO) measures how far the close sits from its moving average, expressed in units of average true range.

concepts.name: Psychological Line
concepts.blurb: The Psychological Line (PSY) measures how often a market closes up, not how far.

concepts.name: QQE
concepts.blurb: QQE (Quantitative Qualitative Estimation) is a smoothed-RSI system with a built-in trailing level.

concepts.name: Qstick
concepts.blurb: Qstick is Tushar Chande's candle-body average: a simple moving average of close minus open over a short lookback.

concepts.name: Rahul Mohindar Oscillator
concepts.blurb: The Rahul Mohindar Oscillator (RMO) is a smoothed momentum gauge developed by Indian trader Rahul Mohindar of Viratech, popularized by its inclusion in MetaStock from the mid-2000s onward.

concepts.name: Rainbow Oscillator
concepts.blurb: The Rainbow Oscillator condenses a rainbow chart, a stack of recursively smoothed moving averages, into a single bounded line.

concepts.name: Reflex/Trendflex
concepts.blurb: Reflex and Trendflex are a pair of oscillators John Ehlers published in 2020, designed to reduce the lag that plagues conventional smoothed momentum tools.

concepts.name: Regular Bullish/bearish Divergence
concepts.blurb: A regular divergence is a disagreement between price extremes and oscillator extremes.

concepts.name: Relative Momentum Index
concepts.blurb: The Relative Momentum Index is Roger Altman's 1993 modification of RSI.

concepts.name: Relative Vigor Index
concepts.blurb: The Relative Vigor Index (RVI) measures the conviction behind price bars by comparing where they close relative to where they open, scaled by their ranges.

concepts.name: ROC
concepts.blurb: ROC, rate of change, is percentage momentum: the current close minus the close n bars ago, divided by that older close, times 100.

concepts.name: ROC-of-ROC
concepts.blurb: ROC-of-ROC applies rate of change twice: it measures how fast the speed of price movement is itself changing.

concepts.name: RSI
concepts.blurb: RSI, the Relative Strength Index, is a bounded momentum oscillator introduced by J. Welles Wilder in his 1978 book New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems.

concepts.name: RSI-2
concepts.blurb: RSI-2 is the standard RSI calculation run with a two-period lookback.

concepts.name: RSI Bands
concepts.blurb: RSI Bands translate RSI thresholds into price.

concepts.name: RSI Failure Swing
concepts.blurb: An RSI failure swing is the reversal pattern Wilder defined on the RSI line itself, without reference to price.

concepts.name: RSI of Other Sources
concepts.blurb: Wilder's RSI is usually described as a price indicator, but the formula is really a general-purpose transform: it takes a series, splits its bar-to-bar changes into gains and losses, smooths each…

concepts.name: RSI Range Rules
concepts.blurb: RSI range rules formalize the observation that RSI does not use its 0-100 scale symmetrically: it shifts its operating range with the trend regime.

concepts.name: Schaff Trend Cycle
concepts.blurb: The Schaff Trend Cycle (STC) is a momentum oscillator developed by currency trader Doug Schaff that runs a stochastic calculation on MACD values instead of price.

concepts.name: Special K
concepts.blurb: The Special K is a momentum indicator developed by Martin Pring that combines short-term, intermediate, and long-term smoothed rate-of-change measurements into a single unbounded line.

concepts.name: Stochastic Momentum Index
concepts.blurb: The Stochastic Momentum Index (SMI), introduced by William Blau in 1993, relocates the stochastic's anchor point.

concepts.name: Stochastic Oscillator
concepts.blurb: The Stochastic Oscillator, developed by George Lane in the 1950s, measures where the latest close sits inside the recent high-low range.

concepts.name: Stochastic Pop
concepts.blurb: A Stochastic Pop deliberately inverts the textbook reading of the stochastic oscillator.

concepts.name: Stochastic RSI
concepts.blurb: The Stochastic RSI applies the stochastic formula to RSI values instead of prices.

concepts.name: Swing Index
concepts.blurb: The Swing Index is J. Welles Wilder's attempt to distill the 'real' price change between two consecutive bars into a single number, using the current bar's open, high, low, and close together with…

concepts.name: Traders Dynamic Index
concepts.blurb: The Traders Dynamic Index (TDI) is a composite momentum indicator, developed by Dean Malone, that layers several readings into one pane.

concepts.name: TRIX
concepts.blurb: TRIX is the one-bar rate of change of a triple-smoothed exponential moving average.

concepts.name: True Strength Index
concepts.blurb: The True Strength Index (TSI) is a momentum oscillator introduced by William Blau.

concepts.name: Ultimate Oscillator
concepts.blurb: The Ultimate Oscillator is Larry Williams's multi-window momentum oscillator, first published in 1985.

concepts.name: Volume-weighted MACD
concepts.blurb: The Volume-weighted MACD swaps the averages inside MACD: instead of subtracting a slow EMA from a fast EMA of price, it subtracts a slow VWMA from a fast VWMA (implementations commonly keep the…

concepts.name: Wave Trend Oscillator
concepts.blurb: The Wave Trend Oscillator is a heavily smoothed momentum oscillator built on the same core as CCI: it measures how far the average price (typically the mean of high, low, and close) sits from an…

concepts.name: Williams %R
concepts.blurb: Williams %R is Larry Williams' momentum oscillator measuring where the latest close sits inside the recent high-low range.

concepts.name: Woodies CCI Conventions
concepts.blurb: Woodies CCI conventions are a rule set for trading the Commodity Channel Index popularized by Ken Wood, a futures trader who built an active online following in the early 2000s.

concepts.name: Zero-lag MACD
concepts.blurb: The Zero-lag MACD is MACD rebuilt on de-lagged averages.

concepts.name: Acceleration Bands
concepts.blurb: Acceleration bands are a price envelope developed by Price Headley in which the band width at each bar is driven by that bar's own high-low range, normalized by its midpoint.

concepts.name: ATR
concepts.blurb: ATR (Average True Range) is J. Welles Wilder's volatility measure, introduced in his 1978 book New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems.

concepts.name: ATR Bands
concepts.blurb: ATR Bands are a volatility envelope built from ATR: take a basis line, usually a simple or exponential moving average of closes (some versions center on price itself), and plot bands a fixed multiple…

concepts.name: ATR-based Stop Distance
concepts.blurb: ATR-based stop distance is the practice of placing a stop-loss a multiple of the ATR away from the entry price, below for longs and above for shorts.

concepts.name: ATR Expansion/contraction
concepts.blurb: ATR expansion/contraction reads the direction of change in ATR, Wilder's smoothed measure of true range.

concepts.name: %B
concepts.blurb: %B is John Bollinger's companion statistic to his bands: it expresses where price sits within Bollinger Bands as a single number, computed as (price - lower band) divided by (upper band - lower band).

concepts.name: Band Walk
concepts.blurb: A band walk is the behavior of price repeatedly closing on or beyond one outer band of a volatility channel, bar after bar, during a strong trend.

concepts.name: BandWidth
concepts.blurb: BandWidth is John Bollinger's normalized measure of how wide Bollinger Bands are: upper band minus lower band, divided by the middle band.

concepts.name: Bollinger Bands
concepts.blurb: Bollinger Bands are a three-line volatility envelope developed by John Bollinger in the early 1980s.

concepts.name: Bollinger Band Tag Reversion
concepts.blurb: A Bollinger Band tag reversion is a mean-reversion setup: price touches or pierces one of the outer Bollinger Bands (by default two standard deviations from a 20-period average) and the trade bets on…

concepts.name: Bollinger Squeeze
concepts.blurb: A Bollinger Squeeze is a volatility contraction read directly off Bollinger Bands.

concepts.name: Chaikin Volatility
concepts.blurb: Chaikin Volatility, developed by Marc Chaikin, measures volatility as the rate of change of the average bar spread.

concepts.name: Choppiness Index
concepts.blurb: The Choppiness Index (CHOP) is a 0-100 gauge of how directional recent price action has been, created by Australian commodity trader E.W. Dreiss.

concepts.name: Close-to-close Historical Volatility
concepts.blurb: Close-to-close historical volatility is the standard deviation of logarithmic returns computed from closing prices, usually annualized and quoted as a percentage.

concepts.name: Damiani Volatmeter
concepts.blurb: The Damiani Volatmeter is a trade/no-trade filter, attributed to Luis Damiani and circulated widely in the MetaTrader forex community in the mid-2000s, that tries to answer one question: is the…

concepts.name: Donchian Channels
concepts.blurb: Donchian Channels plot the highest high and lowest low of the last N bars, usually with a midline halfway between them.

concepts.name: Donchian Width
concepts.blurb: Donchian width is the vertical distance between the upper and lower lines of Donchian channels: the highest high of the last N bars minus the lowest low over the same window.

concepts.name: Double Bollinger Zones
concepts.blurb: Double Bollinger Zones come from running two sets of Bollinger Bands on the same basis, one pair at one standard deviation and one at two, typically around a 20-period SMA.

concepts.name: Envelope
concepts.blurb: An envelope is a pair of boundary lines offset symmetrically above and below a baseline, most commonly a moving average shifted up and down by a fixed percentage: upper = baseline × (1 + p), lower =…

concepts.name: Event-driven Volatility
concepts.blurb: Event-driven volatility is the share of price variability tied to identifiable catalysts: scheduled releases such as central-bank decisions, inflation and employment prints, and earnings, plus…

concepts.name: EWMA Volatility
concepts.blurb: EWMA volatility estimates variance with an exponentially weighted moving average of squared returns: today's estimate equals a decay factor lambda times yesterday's estimate, plus one minus lambda…

concepts.name: Fibonacci Bollinger Bands
concepts.blurb: Fibonacci Bollinger Bands graft the Fibonacci ratio ladder onto a volatility envelope.

concepts.name: Gap-volatility Relation
concepts.blurb: The gap-volatility relation is the two-way link between opening gaps and volatility: gaps are both a component of an instrument's total volatility and a symptom of its current volatility regime.

concepts.name: GARCH-family Clustering
