concepts.blurb: GARCH-family clustering refers to modeling volatility clustering, the well-documented tendency of large returns to follow large returns and calm to follow calm, with GARCH models: generalized…

concepts.name: Garman-Klass Estimator
concepts.blurb: The Garman-Klass estimator computes historical volatility from each bar's open, high, low, and close rather than from closes alone.

concepts.name: Garman-Klass–Yang-Zhang Hybrid
concepts.blurb: The Garman-Klass–Yang-Zhang hybrid (GKYZ) is the Garman-Klass estimator patched for overnight gaps.

concepts.name: Jump Detection
concepts.blurb: Jump detection separates the discontinuous part of price movement, sudden repricings and gaps typically tied to news, from the continuous diffusion-like part.

concepts.name: Kase Studies
concepts.blurb: The Kase studies are a suite of volatility-normalized tools developed in the early 1990s by Cynthia Kase, a chemical engineer turned energy trader.

concepts.name: Keltner Channels
concepts.blurb: Keltner Channels are volatility bands drawn around a moving average with the offset set by average true range: a midline (commonly a 20-period EMA) plus an upper and lower band at the midline plus or…

concepts.name: Mass Index
concepts.blurb: The Mass Index is Donald Dorsey's range-based reversal indicator, introduced in Technical Analysis of Stocks and Commodities in the early 1990s.

concepts.name: NR4/NR7 Narrow-range Bars
concepts.blurb: An NR4 bar is a bar whose high-to-low range is the narrowest of the most recent four bars; an NR7 is the narrowest of the most recent seven.

concepts.name: Parkinson Estimator
concepts.blurb: The Parkinson estimator computes historical volatility from the high-low range: the per-bar variance estimate is the squared natural log of high over low, divided by four times the natural log of…

concepts.name: Projection Bands
concepts.blurb: Projection bands are a channel introduced by Mel Widner in the mid-1990s that projects recent highs and lows forward along their own regression slopes.

concepts.name: Range Expansion/contraction
concepts.blurb: Range expansion and contraction describe the two phases volatility cycles through at the bar level.

concepts.name: Realized Volatility
concepts.blurb: Realized volatility is the volatility an asset actually printed over a past window, computed from observed returns rather than from option prices.

concepts.name: Relative Volatility Index
concepts.blurb: The Relative Volatility Index (RVI) is Donald Dorsey's 1993 oscillator that applies RSI arithmetic to volatility instead of price change.

concepts.name: Rogers-Satchell Estimator
concepts.blurb: The Rogers-Satchell estimator is an OHLC volatility estimator whose defining property is drift independence: it stays unbiased when the market trends, where earlier range-based estimators assume a…

concepts.name: Squeeze Release Direction
concepts.blurb: A squeeze flags compressed volatility and likely expansion, but it is direction-neutral.

concepts.name: Standard-deviation Channel Width
concepts.blurb: Standard-deviation channel width is the distance between the rails of a linear regression channel whose bands are set a multiple of the standard deviation of residuals above and below the fitted line.

concepts.name: STARC Bands
concepts.blurb: STARC bands (Stoller Average Range Channels, developed by Manning Stoller) are a volatility channel: a simple moving average with upper and lower bands offset by a multiple of the average true range.

concepts.name: SVE Bands
concepts.blurb: SVE bands are volatility bands from Sylvain Vervoort, the technical analyst and author of Capturing Profit with Technical Analysis whose studies appeared under the SVE prefix in Technical Analysis of…

concepts.name: The Range Indicator
concepts.blurb: The Range Indicator, often abbreviated TRI, is Jack Weinberg's study comparing each bar's intraday range with the interday change, published in Technical Analysis of Stocks and Commodities in 1995.

concepts.name: TTM Squeeze
concepts.blurb: The TTM Squeeze is a volatility-compression setup popularized by John Carter that combines two band systems into one condition: when Bollinger Bands contract until they trade entirely inside Keltner…

concepts.name: Ulcer Index
concepts.blurb: The Ulcer Index is a downside-risk measure developed in the late 1980s by Peter Martin and Byron McCann, published in their 1989 book The Investor's Guide to Fidelity Funds.

concepts.name: Volatility Cones
concepts.blurb: Volatility cones are a display of how realized volatility has historically been distributed across measurement horizons.

concepts.name: Volatility Contraction Pattern
concepts.blurb: The Volatility Contraction Pattern (VCP) is Mark Minervini's name for a base in which each successive pullback is smaller than the last: a correction of, say, 20% is followed by one near 10%, then…

concepts.name: Volatility Estimators
concepts.blurb: Volatility estimators are the family of formulas that turn a window of price history into a number for realized (historical) volatility.

concepts.name: Volatility of Volatility
concepts.blurb: Volatility of volatility (vol-of-vol) is second-order volatility: a measure of how unstable the volatility series itself is.

concepts.name: Volatility Percentile/rank
concepts.blurb: Volatility percentile/rank normalizes a volatility measure against its own history.

concepts.name: Volatility Ratio
concepts.blurb: The Volatility Ratio compares one volatility reading against a baseline to show, in a single number, whether conditions are unusually active.

concepts.name: Volatility Regime Classification
concepts.blurb: Volatility regime classification assigns each period a discrete volatility state, most commonly low, normal, and high, sometimes with an extra crisis tier, instead of leaving volatility as a…

concepts.name: Volatility Signature Plot
concepts.blurb: A volatility signature plot graphs realized volatility against the sampling frequency used to compute it.

concepts.name: Volatility Switch
concepts.blurb: The Volatility Switch is a bounded volatility-regime gauge proposed by Ron McEwan (Technical Analysis of Stocks & Commodities, 2013).

concepts.name: Volatility Term Structure
concepts.blurb: The volatility term structure is the curve produced by plotting a volatility measure against its horizon.

concepts.name: Waddah Attar Explosion
concepts.blurb: The Waddah Attar Explosion is a momentum-versus-volatility gate that emerged from the forex trading community, named after its creator, Waddah Attar.

concepts.name: Weekend/overnight Volatility Profile
concepts.blurb: A weekend/overnight volatility profile is a statistical study of how much price movement occurs while a market is closed or thinly traded, compared with its regular hours.

concepts.name: Yang-Zhang Estimator
concepts.blurb: The Yang-Zhang estimator is a realized-volatility estimator for OHLC bars, published by Dennis Yang and Qiang Zhang in 2000.

concepts.name: 80% Rule
concepts.blurb: The 80% rule, also called the value-area rule, is a Market Profile trading guideline: when price opens outside the prior session's value area and then re-enters it and holds inside, the market has a…

concepts.name: Absorption & Exhaustion
concepts.blurb: Absorption and exhaustion are the two classic order-flow explanations for why a directional move stalls.

concepts.name: Accumulation/Distribution Line
concepts.blurb: The Accumulation/Distribution Line is a cumulative volume-flow indicator created by Marc Chaikin, the Wall Street analyst whose name also attaches to the Chaikin Oscillator and Chaikin Money Flow,…

concepts.name: Anchored VWAP
concepts.blurb: Anchored VWAP (AVWAP) is a volume-weighted average price whose calculation starts at a bar you choose rather than at an automatic boundary such as the session open.

concepts.name: Auction Failure
concepts.blurb: Auction failure is the Market Profile term for a directional probe that fails to do its job.

concepts.name: Auction Open/close Imbalances
concepts.blurb: Auction open/close imbalances are the published excess of buy or sell interest heading into an exchange's opening or closing auction.

concepts.name: Balance vs Imbalance
concepts.blurb: Balance vs imbalance is the core distinction of auction market theory, from the Market Profile tradition begun by J. Peter Steidlmayer.

concepts.name: Better Volume Classifications
concepts.blurb: Better Volume classifications are a bar-labeling scheme that sorts each bar into a volume archetype using three inputs: volume, the bar's range (spread), and the close.

concepts.name: Bid/ask Imbalance
concepts.blurb: A bid/ask imbalance is a footprint chart reading that flags price levels where one side traded far more aggressively than the other.

concepts.name: Bill Williams Market Facilitation Index
concepts.blurb: The Bill Williams Market Facilitation Index (BW MFI) measures how much price movement each unit of volume produced: the bar's high minus its low, divided by its volume.

concepts.name: Block Trades
concepts.blurb: A block trade is a single transaction of institutional size, large enough that exchanges and regulators treat it as its own category.

concepts.name: Chaikin Money Flow
concepts.blurb: Chaikin Money Flow (CMF) is a volume-weighted oscillator developed by Marc Chaikin that measures buying and selling pressure over a rolling window, typically 20 or 21 bars.

concepts.name: Chaikin Oscillator
concepts.blurb: The Chaikin Oscillator, developed by Marc Chaikin, measures the momentum of the Accumulation/Distribution Line by subtracting a slower EMA of that line from a faster one, conventionally the 10-period…

concepts.name: Churn
concepts.blurb: Churn is heavy trading volume that produces little or no price progress: the market works hard and goes nowhere.

concepts.name: Climactic Action
concepts.blurb: Climactic action is the volume-spread-analysis term for the violent end of a trend: a bar or short burst of bars with ultra-high volume and unusually wide range after an extended move, where…

concepts.name: Cumulative Volume Delta
concepts.blurb: Cumulative volume delta (CVD) is a running total of volume delta, the difference between volume traded aggressively at the ask (market buys) and volume traded aggressively at the bid (market sells).

concepts.name: Day-type Taxonomy
concepts.blurb: The day-type taxonomy is the Market Profile classification of trading sessions by how far and how convincingly price extends beyond the initial balance, the range of the first hour.

concepts.name: Delta Divergence
concepts.blurb: Delta divergence is a disagreement between price and the aggression behind it.

concepts.name: Delta Profile
concepts.blurb: A delta profile is a price-by-price histogram of net aggression.

concepts.name: Demand Index
concepts.blurb: The Demand Index is a composite indicator developed by James Sibbet that combines price change and volume into a single measure of buying pressure relative to selling pressure.

concepts.name: DOM
concepts.blurb: The DOM (depth of market) is the live order book displayed as a price ladder: the size of resting limit orders at each level on the bid side and the ask side, often ten or so levels each way…

concepts.name: Ease of Movement
concepts.blurb: Ease of Movement (EOM, sometimes EMV) is a volume-based oscillator developed by Richard W. Arms Jr., the analyst also behind Equivolume charting, that measures how easily price is moving relative to…

concepts.name: Excess
concepts.blurb: Excess is the Market Profile term for the footprint left when an auction travels too far and is decisively rejected: a tail of prices at a session or swing extreme that traded only briefly before…

concepts.name: Execution Algo Footprints
concepts.blurb: Execution algo footprints are the recurring traces that institutional execution algorithms leave in the tape and the order book.

concepts.name: Footprint Concepts
concepts.blurb: A footprint chart replaces each candle with a ladder of prices and shows, at every price, how much volume traded at the bid versus at the ask (a bid×ask split).

concepts.name: Force Index
concepts.blurb: The Force Index is Alexander Elder's volume-weighted momentum measure, introduced in his 1993 book Trading for a Living.

concepts.name: Herrick Payoff Index
concepts.blurb: The Herrick Payoff Index (HPI) is a futures-specific indicator, attributed to John Herrick, that combines price change, volume, and open interest into a single smoothed measure of money flowing into…

concepts.name: High/low-volume Nodes
concepts.blurb: High-volume nodes (HVNs) and low-volume nodes (LVNs) are the peaks and troughs of a volume profile, the histogram of volume traded at each price over a chosen range.

concepts.name: Iceberg Detection
concepts.blurb: Iceberg detection is the practice of inferring hidden order size at a price level from the way visible liquidity behaves.

concepts.name: Initial Balance
concepts.blurb: In Market Profile, the initial balance is the price range established at the start of the regular session, classically the first hour of trade, meaning the first two 30-minute periods of a TPO…

concepts.name: Intraday Intensity
concepts.blurb: Intraday Intensity is a volume-pressure gauge developed by David Bostian and popularized by John Bollinger.

concepts.name: Klinger Volume Oscillator
concepts.blurb: The Klinger Volume Oscillator (KVO) is a volume-flow oscillator developed by Stephen Klinger in the 1990s.

concepts.name: Manipulation Footprints
concepts.blurb: Manipulation footprints are the observable traces left in the order book and the tape by illegal or deceptive order activity, chiefly spoofing, layering, and quote stuffing.

concepts.name: Midpoint/half-back of Session
concepts.blurb: The session midpoint, called half-back in futures floor slang, is the halfway point of a session's range: the session high plus the session low, divided by two.

concepts.name: Money Flow Index
concepts.blurb: The Money Flow Index (MFI) is a volume-weighted momentum oscillator bounded between 0 and 100, developed by Gene Quong and Avrum Soudack and often described as a volume-weighted RSI.

concepts.name: Naked POC
concepts.blurb: A naked POC (also called a virgin POC, or NPOC) is a prior session's point of control that price has not traded back through since that session ended.

concepts.name: Negative Volume Index
concepts.blurb: The Negative Volume Index (NVI) is a cumulative line that changes only on sessions when volume falls below the prior session's volume.

concepts.name: No-demand / No-supply Bars
concepts.blurb: No-demand and no-supply bars are classifications from Volume Spread Analysis (VSA), the discipline Tom Williams developed out of Wyckoff's effort vs result logic.

concepts.name: OBV
concepts.blurb: OBV (on-balance volume) is a cumulative volume line introduced by Joe Granville in 1963.

concepts.name: OBV Divergence
concepts.blurb: OBV divergence is a disagreement between price and On-Balance Volume, the running total that adds a bar's entire volume when it closes above the prior close and subtracts it when it closes below.

concepts.name: One-timeframing
concepts.blurb: One-timeframing is auction-theory shorthand, spread through the Market Profile work of Dalton and others, for a market that keeps attacking one side without ever violating the other.

concepts.name: Open Types
concepts.blurb: Open types are the Market Profile taxonomy for how a session begins, popularized by Dalton's auction-theory work.

concepts.name: Order-book Imbalance
concepts.blurb: Order-book imbalance measures the asymmetry between resting buy and sell liquidity in the limit order book.

concepts.name: Periodic VWAPs
concepts.blurb: Periodic VWAPs are volume-weighted average price lines anchored to the start of standard calendar periods: the week, month, quarter, or year.

concepts.name: Pocket Pivot
concepts.blurb: A pocket pivot is a volume-based early-entry signal from the O'Neil tradition, defined by Gil Morales and Chris Kacher.

concepts.name: Point of Control
concepts.blurb: The point of control (POC) is the price at which the most volume traded within a volume profile: the longest row of the histogram, the mode of the period's volume distribution.

concepts.name: Poor High/poor Low
concepts.blurb: A poor high or poor low is a Market Profile judgment on the quality of a session extreme.

concepts.name: Positive Volume Index
concepts.blurb: The Positive Volume Index (PVI) is the mirror of the Negative Volume Index: a cumulative line that updates only on sessions when volume rises above the prior session's volume, moving by that day's…

concepts.name: Price Volume Trend
concepts.blurb: Price Volume Trend (PVT), also written as volume price trend, is a cumulative volume line that adds or subtracts a slice of each bar's volume in proportion to the bar's percentage price change.

concepts.name: Price Zone Oscillator
concepts.blurb: The Price Zone Oscillator (PZO) is a momentum oscillator introduced by Walid Khalil and David Steckler as the price-based companion to their Volume Zone Oscillator.

concepts.name: Profile Shape Taxonomy
concepts.blurb: Profile shape taxonomy is the practice of classifying a session's volume profile or TPO profile by its overall silhouette, and reading each shape as a distinct auction story.

concepts.name: PVO
concepts.blurb: The PVO, or percentage volume oscillator, measures the momentum of volume itself.

concepts.name: Relative Volume
concepts.blurb: Relative volume (RVOL) expresses current volume as a multiple of what is normal for that symbol at that time.

concepts.name: Responsive vs Initiative Activity
concepts.blurb: Responsive versus initiative activity is the Market Profile framework for classifying who is trading and why, based on where activity occurs relative to the previous session's value area.

concepts.name: Resting Liquidity / Liquidity Heatmap
concepts.blurb: Resting liquidity is every order parked in the market rather than chasing it: passive limit orders sitting in the order book waiting for price to come to them, plus the stop orders clustered beyond…

concepts.name: Rolling VWAP
concepts.blurb: A rolling VWAP is a volume-weighted average price computed over a sliding window of fixed length, such as the last 24 hours, the last 7 days, or the last N bars: the sum of price times volume across…

concepts.name: Rotation Factor
concepts.blurb: The rotation factor is a day-timeframe statistic from Market Profile, the auction framework J. Peter Steidlmayer developed at the Chicago Board of Trade.

concepts.name: Session VWAP
concepts.blurb: Session VWAP is the volume-weighted average price of everything traded since the session open, reset at the start of each new session.

concepts.name: Single Prints
concepts.blurb: Single prints are price levels in a TPO profile that traded during only one time bracket, leaving the profile exactly one letter wide there.

concepts.name: Smart Money Index
concepts.blurb: The Smart Money Index (SMI) is a cumulative sentiment line for stock indexes, usually credited to money manager Don Hays.

concepts.name: Stopping Volume
concepts.blurb: Stopping volume is a volume spread analysis term, from the Wyckoff-derived tradition Tom Williams systematized, for the moment heavy volume halts a decline.

concepts.name: Strength/weakness Background
concepts.blurb: The strength/weakness background is a volume spread analysis (VSA) convention: instead of judging each bar in isolation, the analyst maintains a running verdict on whether recent action has printed…

concepts.name: Sweep Detection
concepts.blurb: Sweep detection is the order-flow practice of reconstructing sweeps from the tape: aggressive executions that consume resting liquidity across several price levels almost simultaneously.

concepts.name: Tape Reading
concepts.blurb: Tape reading is the practice of interpreting the stream of executed trades (time and sales) as they print: each entry shows price, size, and time, and most platforms infer from the prevailing quote…

concepts.name: TPO Profile
concepts.blurb: A TPO profile, short for Time Price Opportunity and better known as Market Profile, organizes a session by time spent at each price.

concepts.name: Trade Volume Index
concepts.blurb: The Trade Volume Index (TVI) is a cumulative volume indicator designed for intraday and tick data that classifies each trade or price update as buying or selling based on the direction of the price…

concepts.name: Twiggs Money Flow
concepts.blurb: Twiggs Money Flow (TMF) is Colin Twiggs' refinement of Chaikin Money Flow, which itself builds on the close-location logic of the Accumulation/Distribution Line.

concepts.name: Unfinished Auction
concepts.blurb: An unfinished auction is a directional move that ended without the signature of proper completion.

concepts.name: Unfinished Business
concepts.blurb: Unfinished business is an auction-theory label for a price extreme that formed without a proper ending.

concepts.name: Up/down Volume Ratio
concepts.blurb: The up/down volume ratio compares volume transacted on strength against volume transacted on weakness.

concepts.name: Value Area
concepts.blurb: The value area is the price band containing a set share of a period's trade, 70% by convention.

concepts.name: Value Migration
concepts.blurb: Value migration is the day-over-day tracking of where the market's value area is building relative to the previous session's, used in Market Profile analysis as the primary evidence of directional…

concepts.name: Volume at Breakout
concepts.blurb: Volume at breakout is the practice of judging a breakout by the participation behind it: comparing the volume on the bar that clears a range, level, or pattern boundary, and on the bars immediately…

concepts.name: Volume Delta
concepts.blurb: Volume delta is the difference between buying and selling volume within a bar, where buying means trades executed by lifting the offer and selling means trades hitting the bid.

concepts.name: Volume Divergence
concepts.blurb: Volume divergence is a disagreement between price movement and the participation behind it: price presses to a new high or low while the volume fueling each successive push contracts.

concepts.name: Volume Dry-up
concepts.blurb: A volume dry-up is a contraction in turnover to well below the instrument's recent norm, typically late in a consolidation.

concepts.name: Volume Flow Indicator
concepts.blurb: The Volume Flow Indicator (VFI) is a volume-flow oscillator introduced by Markos Katsanos in 2004 as a refinement of the cumulative flow-line family that includes OBV and volume price trend.

concepts.name: Volume Oscillator
concepts.blurb: The Volume Oscillator measures whether trading activity is expanding or contracting.

concepts.name: Volume Price Trend
concepts.blurb: Volume price trend (VPT, also called price volume trend or PVT) is a cumulative volume line: each bar adds the bar's volume multiplied by the percentage change in close, so the running total rises on…

concepts.name: Volume Profile
concepts.blurb: A volume profile is a histogram of traded volume organized by price instead of time.

concepts.name: Volume Spike
concepts.blurb: A volume spike is a bar that trades dramatically more volume than its recent norm.

concepts.name: Volume Zone Oscillator
concepts.blurb: The Volume Zone Oscillator (VZO) is a bounded volume oscillator introduced by Walid Khalil and David Steckler in 2009.

concepts.name: VSA Test Bar
concepts.blurb: A test bar is a volume spread analysis (VSA) signal in which price dips into an area where supply previously appeared, on a narrow spread and noticeably low volume, and closes in the middle or upper…

concepts.name: VWAP Bands
concepts.blurb: VWAP bands are envelopes drawn above and below a volume-weighted average price line.

concepts.name: VWAP Mean-reversion vs Trend Regimes
concepts.blurb: VWAP mean-reversion vs trend regimes is the observation that the same session VWAP supports two opposite playbooks depending on the day's condition.

concepts.name: VWAP Pinch
concepts.blurb: A VWAP pinch is the compression that forms when two anchored VWAP lines converge with price squeezed between them, a read popularized by Brian Shannon.

concepts.name: Weis Wave Volume
concepts.blurb: Weis Wave Volume is a Wyckoff-lineage tool developed by David Weis that organizes volume by swing instead of by bar.

concepts.name: Williams A/D
concepts.blurb: Williams A/D (Williams Accumulation/Distribution) is a cumulative running line developed by trader Larry Williams that adds a measure of buying pressure on up-closes and subtracts a measure of…

concepts.name: 1-2-3 Reversal
concepts.blurb: A 1-2-3 reversal is a three-point trend-change pattern.

concepts.name: Accumulation vs Distribution Ranges
concepts.blurb: In Wyckoff-derived analysis, a sideways range is not neutral ground: it is where large participants build or unload positions while price is contained.

concepts.name: Break of Structure
concepts.blurb: A break of structure (BOS) is a with-trend structural break.

concepts.name: Breakout-pullback-continuation
concepts.blurb: Breakout-pullback-continuation is the three-phase sequence behind the classic break-and-retest trade: a breakout through a level, a pullback that returns to test the level from the other side, and a…

concepts.name: Change of Character
concepts.blurb: A change of character (CHoCH) is the first structural break against the prevailing trend: in an uptrend, price breaking the most recent meaningful higher low; in a downtrend, breaking the most recent…

concepts.name: Compression Into Level
concepts.blurb: Compression into a level is a stair-stepping approach to support or resistance: instead of one clean impulse, price grinds toward the level in progressively smaller swings, leaving a chain of…

concepts.name: Corrective Leg
concepts.blurb: A corrective leg is the counter-directional segment of market structure: after an impulse leg expands with the trend, the corrective leg is the slower, overlapping move that retraces part of it.

concepts.name: Deviation Above/below Range
concepts.blurb: A deviation is a move that leaves an established trading range, trades above its high or below its low, fails to find acceptance, and closes back inside.

concepts.name: Dow Theory
concepts.blurb: Dow Theory is widely regarded as the oldest codified branch of Western technical analysis: a set of principles describing how market trends form, persist, and reverse.

concepts.name: Expansion → Retracement → Consolidation Cycle
concepts.blurb: The expansion → retracement → consolidation cycle is the rhythm many structure traders assume price repeats: a directional impulse leg expands the range, a corrective leg gives part of it back, and…

concepts.name: False Breakout
concepts.blurb: A false breakout (or fakeout) is a breakout that fails: price pushes through a level the market visibly treats as a boundary, a trading range extreme, a support or resistance level, or a well-watched…

concepts.name: Fractal Nesting
concepts.blurb: Fractal nesting is the observation that market structure is self-similar across degrees: every swing at one scale is built out of complete smaller swing sequences at the scale below.

concepts.name: Impulse Leg
concepts.blurb: An impulse leg is the directional segment of market structure: the fast, one-sided move that travels with the prevailing trend and does the structural work of taking out prior swing points.

concepts.name: Internal vs External Structure
concepts.blurb: External structure is the market's major swing skeleton: the significant swing highs and lows that define the current trend or range at the degree being analyzed.

concepts.name: Livermore Pivotal Point
concepts.blurb: A Livermore pivotal point is the price at which, in Jesse Livermore's method, the real trend of a stock is decided.

concepts.name: Measured Move
concepts.blurb: A measured move is a price projection built on the tendency of trends to unfold in legs of similar size.

concepts.name: Multi-timeframe Structure Alignment
concepts.blurb: Multi-timeframe structure alignment is the practice of requiring the swing structure of two or more timeframes to agree before acting.

concepts.name: Parabolic Phase
concepts.blurb: A parabolic phase is the terminal stage of a strong trend in which price stops advancing linearly and begins to curve: each successive leg is steeper and faster than the last, pullbacks shrink or…

concepts.name: Pivot Strength
concepts.blurb: Pivot strength is the bar-count rule that defines a swing point: a pivot high of strength N is a bar whose high exceeds the highs of the N bars to its left and the N bars to its right, with the…

concepts.name: Re-accumulation
concepts.blurb: Re-accumulation is a pause in an established uptrend during which large participants absorb supply and rebuild positions before the trend resumes higher.

concepts.name: Re-distribution
concepts.blurb: Re-distribution is a pause in an established downtrend during which larger sellers rebuild short positions or unload remaining inventory before the decline resumes.

concepts.name: Strong vs Weak Swings
concepts.blurb: Strong vs weak swings is Smart Money Concepts vocabulary for grading swing points by what they accomplished.

concepts.name: Structure Invalidation
concepts.blurb: Structure invalidation is the event that proves a structural trade thesis wrong: price decisively takes out the swing point on which the thesis depends.

concepts.name: Swing Failure Pattern
concepts.blurb: A swing failure pattern (SFP) is a failed raid on a prior swing point.

concepts.name: Swing High/low
concepts.blurb: A swing high is a bar whose high stands above the highs of a set number of bars on either side; a swing low is the mirror image, a low beneath its neighbors' lows.

concepts.name: Swing Magnitude Filters
concepts.blurb: A swing magnitude filter is a minimum-size rule applied to swing detection: a move only counts as a new structural leg if it travels at least a threshold distance from the prior extreme.

concepts.name: Swing Structure Grammar
concepts.blurb: Swing structure grammar is the labeling system that turns a series of swing highs and lows into a trend statement.

concepts.name: Trading Range
concepts.blurb: A trading range is a sideways stretch of price contained between a defined high and a defined low: repeated tests of a ceiling that sells and a floor that buys, with neither side able to force a…

concepts.name: Turtle Soup
concepts.blurb: Turtle Soup is a failed-breakout reversal setup published by Laurence Connors and Linda Raschke in Street Smarts (1995), named at the expense of the Turtles, the trend-following group trained by…

concepts.name: Williams Fractal
concepts.blurb: A Williams Fractal is a five-bar swing marker popularized by Bill Williams in his Trading Chaos work.

concepts.name: Zigzag Structure
concepts.blurb: A zigzag reduces price action to a sequence of alternating up and down legs.

concepts.name: Accumulation-manipulation-distribution
concepts.blurb: Accumulation–manipulation–distribution (AMD), or in ICT vocabulary the Power of Three (PO3), is a template for how a trading period unfolds around its open.

concepts.name: Balanced Price Range
concepts.blurb: A balanced price range (BPR) is the overlap of two opposing fair value gaps.

concepts.name: Breaker Block
concepts.blurb: A breaker block is an order block that failed and flipped roles.

concepts.name: Bullish/bearish Order Block
concepts.blurb: An order block is the last candle that closed against a move before the move took off.

concepts.name: Buy-side Liquidity
concepts.blurb: Buy-side liquidity, usually shortened to BSL, is the pool of resting buy orders above a visible high: the protective stops of short sellers plus the stop-entries of breakout traders.

concepts.name: Change in State of Delivery
concepts.blurb: A change in the state of delivery (CISD) is ICT's body-close test for the moment price flips from being delivered in one direction to the other.

concepts.name: Consequent Encroachment
concepts.blurb: Consequent encroachment (usually just CE) is the midpoint of a fair value gap: the 50% line between the gap's boundaries.

concepts.name: Displacement
concepts.blurb: Displacement is a fast, one-sided move: a run of large-bodied candles closing in the same direction that covers ground quickly and typically leaves a fair value gap or two behind.

concepts.name: Draw on Liquidity
concepts.blurb: The draw on liquidity (DOL) is the level a market is currently reaching for: the pool of resting orders acting as the magnet for price delivery.

concepts.name: Equal Highs/lows As Liquidity
concepts.blurb: Equal highs are two or more swing highs stalling at nearly the same price; equal lows are the mirror image.

concepts.name: Fair Value Gap
concepts.blurb: A fair value gap is a three-candle imbalance.

concepts.name: FVG Behavior Rules
concepts.blurb: FVG behavior rules are the conventions Smart Money Concepts / ICT traders layer on top of the basic fair value gap definition to decide which gaps matter and what price is expected to do with them.

concepts.name: ICT Macros
concepts.blurb: ICT macros are short, recurring windows of the trading day in which ICT teaching expects a concentrated burst of price delivery — canonically the xx:50–xx:10 shape, opening ten minutes before the top…

concepts.name: ICT Session Ranges
concepts.blurb: ICT session ranges are fixed evening windows, clocked in New York time, whose highs and lows become measuring tools for the following trading day.

concepts.name: ICT Time Anchors
concepts.blurb: ICT time anchors are fixed New York-time reference points the ICT framework hangs the trading day on: chiefly the midnight open (00:00 New York time), which begins the "true day," and the 8:30 open,…

concepts.name: Immediate Rebalance
concepts.blurb: An immediate rebalance is the opposite outcome to a fair value gap.

concepts.name: Implied FVG
concepts.blurb: An implied fair value gap is the wick-built cousin of the standard three-candle imbalance.

concepts.name: Inducement
concepts.blurb: Inducement (marked IDM on many charts) is liquidity read as bait: in the common usage, the minor pullback high or low sitting in front of a level a larger move is expected to reach.

concepts.name: Institutional Order Flow
concepts.blurb: Institutional order flow is the ICT term for the market's prevailing direction of delivery: the sustained directional pressure attributed to large participants, inferred entirely from price behavior.

concepts.name: Internal vs External Range Liquidity
concepts.blurb: Internal and external range liquidity split targets by where they sit relative to the current dealing range — a swing low to a swing high (or the reverse), usually drawn on a higher timeframe.

concepts.name: Inversion FVG
concepts.blurb: An inversion fair value gap is a fair value gap that failed and flipped roles.

concepts.name: IPDA & Price Delivery Theory
concepts.blurb: IPDA, the Interbank Price Delivery Algorithm, is the ICT premise that price is delivered rather than merely discovered: moved with intent between pools of resting liquidity on one side and…

concepts.name: Judas Swing
concepts.blurb: A Judas swing is ICT's name for the false move early in a session: a push in one direction, usually shortly after a session open, that runs resting stops before the day's real move develops the other…

concepts.name: Killzones
concepts.blurb: Killzones are the windows of the trading day when ICT (Inner Circle Trader) methodology expects institutional participation, and therefore tradeable displacement, to concentrate.

concepts.name: Liquidity Pool
concepts.blurb: A liquidity pool is a price region where resting orders are assumed to cluster: stop-losses and pending breakout entries stacked just beyond an obvious reference point.

concepts.name: Liquidity Sweep
concepts.blurb: A liquidity sweep is a run through a level where resting orders cluster — the stop-losses and breakout entries sitting just beyond an obvious high or low.

concepts.name: Low-resistance vs High-resistance Liquidity Runs
concepts.blurb: Low-resistance and high-resistance liquidity runs describe how easily price travels toward a pool of resting orders.

concepts.name: Market Maker Models
concepts.blurb: Market maker models are the ICT schematic for a complete delivery cycle.

concepts.name: Mitigation Block
concepts.blurb: A mitigation block is an order-block variant from Inner Circle Trader (ICT) vocabulary.

concepts.name: Model 2022
concepts.blurb: Model 2022 is the intraday entry model taught in the free 2022 ICT YouTube mentorship — the community adopted the year as the model's name.

concepts.name: New Day Opening Gap
concepts.blurb: A new day opening gap (NDOG) is the span between one trading day's closing print and the next day's opening print.

concepts.name: New Week Opening Gap
concepts.blurb: A new week opening gap (NWOG) is the span between Friday's closing price and the new week's opening price: for markets that trade essentially around the clock during the week, like index futures and…

concepts.name: One-shot-one-kill
concepts.blurb: One Shot One Kill (OSOK) is an ICT weekly-range model built on sniper discipline: frame one directional idea for the week, take one precision entry, and stand down.

concepts.name: Opening Gap
concepts.blurb: An opening gap is the span between one session's close and the next session's open — untraded not because price moved too fast, but because the market was shut.

concepts.name: Optimal Trade Entry
concepts.blurb: Optimal trade entry is the ICT name for a specific retracement band: the span between the 61.8% and 79% pullback of an impulse leg, with 70.5% (the midpoint) often marked as the sweet spot.

concepts.name: Order Block Anatomy & Refinement
concepts.blurb: An order block is the last opposing candle before a displacing move (the final down candle before an impulsive rally, or the final up candle before a markdown), read as the footprint of the orders…

concepts.name: PD Arrays
concepts.blurb: PD arrays (premium/discount arrays) are ICT's collective name for the reference points a market leaves behind as it trades: old highs and lows, order blocks, fair value gaps, liquidity voids,…

concepts.name: Premium & Discount
concepts.blurb: Premium and discount is the SMC/ICT convention for pricing a range.

concepts.name: Propulsion Block
concepts.blurb: A propulsion block is an ICT order-block variant: a candle that trades back into a prior order block, respects it, and drives away, becoming a tradable block in its own right.

concepts.name: Quarterly Theory
concepts.blurb: Quarterly Theory divides every trading cycle into four quarters and gives each a role.

concepts.name: Reclaimed Order Block
concepts.blurb: A reclaimed order block is an order block that has already served once and is later revisited and used again in its original direction.

concepts.name: Rejection Block
concepts.blurb: A rejection block is the ICT array built from a wick rather than a candle body.

concepts.name: Seek & Destroy Profile
concepts.blurb: The seek-and-destroy profile is ICT's name for a day that runs both sides and rewards neither: price pushes above a recent high to take buy stops, rotates down through a recent low to take sell…

concepts.name: Sell-side Liquidity
concepts.blurb: Sell-side liquidity (SSL) is the pool of sell orders resting below prior lows (the protective stops of longs plus the entries of breakout sellers).

concepts.name: Session Liquidity
concepts.blurb: Session liquidity is the resting-order pool that builds at the high and low of each major trading session.

concepts.name: Session & Weekly Profiles
concepts.blurb: Session and weekly profiles are recurring templates for how a trading day or week tends to unfold against the session clock.

concepts.name: Silver Bullet
concepts.blurb: The Silver Bullet is an ICT setup defined by the clock: a specific one-hour window in which the trader looks for a single trade.

concepts.name: Smart Money Concepts
concepts.blurb: Smart Money Concepts (SMC) is a price-action trading methodology built on one central claim: large institutional participants, the so-called smart money, move markets in ways that leave repeatable…

concepts.name: Smart Money Reversal
concepts.blurb: A smart money reversal is the turn that follows a liquidity grab: price runs through a level where resting orders collect (an old high or low, equal highs or lows) and instead of continuing,…

concepts.name: Smart Money Technique Divergence
concepts.blurb: Smart Money Technique (SMT) divergence is a non-confirmation between two correlated instruments at matching swing points.

concepts.name: Standard-deviation Projections
concepts.blurb: Standard-deviation projections extend the height of a completed range in multiples above and below it, mapping where a later expansion might reach.

concepts.name: Trendline Liquidity
concepts.blurb: Trendline liquidity is the pool of resting orders that accumulates around a widely drawn trendline.

concepts.name: Unicorn
concepts.blurb: The unicorn is an ICT entry model defined by one specific confluence: a breaker block overlapping a fair value gap.

concepts.name: Volume Imbalance
concepts.blurb: A volume imbalance is a gap between the real bodies of two consecutive candles: the first candle's close and the next candle's open leave a span that only wicks traded through.

concepts.name: Absorption
concepts.blurb: Absorption is what happens when aggressive orders pour into a price level and the level holds anyway: resting passive orders take everything thrown at them, so volume prints heavily while price makes…

concepts.name: Cause & Effect
concepts.blurb: Cause and effect is one of the three fundamental laws of the Wyckoff Method, alongside supply and demand and effort vs result.

concepts.name: Composite Man
concepts.blurb: The Composite Man, also called the composite operator, is Richard Wyckoff's teaching device for reading a market as if every large, informed interest were a single fictional operator running one…

concepts.name: Effort vs Result
concepts.blurb: Effort vs result is the third of Wyckoff's three laws.

concepts.name: Markup & Markdown
concepts.blurb: Markup and markdown are the two trending phases of the Wyckoff market cycle, the four-stage sequence of accumulation, markup, distribution, and markdown that the Wyckoff Method uses to describe how…

concepts.name: Nine Buying/selling Tests
concepts.blurb: The nine buying tests and nine selling tests are checklists from the Wyckoff tradition used to judge whether an accumulation base is ready to support markup, or a distribution top is ready to break…

concepts.name: Point & Figure Cause Counting
concepts.blurb: Point & Figure cause counting, often just called the horizontal count, is the Wyckoff technique of measuring the width of a completed trading range on a point & figure chart and projecting that width…

concepts.name: Re-accumulation vs Re-distribution Diagnosis
concepts.blurb: Re-accumulation vs re-distribution diagnosis is the Wyckoff discipline of deciding what a consolidation inside an existing trend actually is: a pause where the campaign adds to positions before…

concepts.name: Spring
concepts.blurb: A spring is a Wyckoff event at the bottom of an accumulation trading range: price breaks below the range's support, finds little further selling, and quickly reverses back inside.

concepts.name: Supply & Demand
concepts.blurb: The law of supply and demand is the first of the three laws underpinning the Wyckoff Method: when demand exceeds supply, price rises; when supply exceeds demand, price falls; when the two are roughly…

concepts.name: Trading-range Position
concepts.blurb: Trading-range position is the discipline of locating where price currently sits inside a trading range, near support, near resistance, or in the middle, and letting that location govern what trades…

concepts.name: Upthrust
concepts.blurb: An upthrust is the bearish mirror of the spring: price pushes above the resistance of a trading range, finds no real demand, and falls back inside.

concepts.name: Upthrust After Distribution
concepts.blurb: An upthrust after distribution, usually abbreviated UTAD, is the terminal false breakout in the Wyckoff distribution model: a push above the resistance of a distribution range, late in the structure,…

concepts.name: Wyckoff Accumulation Schematic
concepts.blurb: The Wyckoff Accumulation Schematic is the idealized map of how a downtrend ends and a new uptrend is prepared.

concepts.name: Wyckoff Distribution Schematic
concepts.blurb: The Wyckoff Distribution Schematic is the mirror of the Wyckoff Accumulation Schematic: the idealized map of how an uptrend is ended and a markdown prepared.

concepts.name: Wyckoff Method
concepts.blurb: The Wyckoff Method is a technical analysis framework built on a single premise: large, well-financed operators move markets in campaigns, and their activity leaves readable footprints in price and…

concepts.name: Wyckoff Wave & Volume Studies
concepts.blurb: Wyckoff Wave & Volume Studies read the market as alternating buying and selling waves instead of fixed-time bars.
The 5-0 is a five-point harmonic structure defined by Scott Carney, distinctive because it begins with a failed trend rather than a clean retracement.

concepts.name: ABCD
concepts.blurb: The ABCD, often written AB=CD, is the simplest of the harmonic patterns: two price legs of matching length separated by a correction.

concepts.name: Anti-patterns
concepts.blurb: Anti-patterns are mirrored-ratio counterparts of the classic XABCD harmonic patterns: the anti-Gartley, anti-Bat, anti-Butterfly, anti-Crab, and anti-Cypher.

concepts.name: Bat

concepts.name: Butterfly
concepts.blurb: The Butterfly is an XABCD harmonic extension pattern associated with Bryce Gilmore and Larry Pesavento: unlike the Gartley or Bat, its D point completes beyond the X extreme.

concepts.name: Combination Corrections

concepts.name: Corrective Wave
concepts.blurb: A corrective wave is Elliott wave theory's countertrend unit: the move that partially retraces a preceding motive wave and travels against the trend one degree larger.

concepts.name: Crab
concepts.blurb: The Crab is the most extended of the standard XABCD harmonic patterns, introduced by Scott Carney in 2000.

concepts.name: Diagonals
concepts.blurb: Diagonals are the wedge-shaped members of the motive family in Elliott wave analysis: five-wave structures that move in the direction of the one-larger trend but violate the normal impulse rule…

concepts.name: Elliott Guidelines
concepts.blurb: Elliott guidelines are the tendencies of Elliott Wave Theory, distinct from its three hard rules.

concepts.name: Elliott Hard Rules

concepts.name: Elliott Wave Theory
concepts.blurb: Elliott Wave Theory is a branch of technical analysis built on the idea that crowd psychology moves markets in recognizable, repeating wave patterns.

concepts.name: Exotic Harmonics

concepts.name: Fib Wave Relationships
concepts.blurb: Fib wave relationships are the Fibonacci proportions Elliott practitioners use to relate waves to one another: guidelines for how long a wave tends to be relative to the waves before it.

concepts.name: Flat
concepts.blurb: A flat is a sideways corrective structure in Elliott wave analysis, subdividing 3-3-5: wave A is a three, wave B is a three that retraces most or all of A, and wave C is a five.

concepts.name: Gartley
concepts.blurb: The Gartley is a five-point XABCD retracement pattern first sketched by H.M. Gartley in his 1935 book Profits in the Stock Market, on page 222, which is why it is also called the 222 pattern.

concepts.name: Harmonic & Fib Ratio Set
concepts.blurb: The Harmonic & Fib Ratio Set is the shared vocabulary of levels behind Fibonacci tools and harmonic patterns: 0.382, 0.5, 0.618, 0.707, 0.786, 0.886, 1.13, 1.272, 1.414, 1.618, 2.0, 2.24, 2.618,…

concepts.name: Harmonic Patterns
concepts.blurb: Harmonic patterns are multi-leg chart formations, usually drawn across five swing points labeled X, A, B, C, and D, in which each leg must relate to the others through specific Fibonacci ratios.

concepts.name: Impulse
concepts.blurb: An impulse is the five-wave engine of Elliott wave theory: a move in the direction of the next larger trend that subdivides 1-2-3-4-5, with waves 1, 3, and 5 advancing and waves 2 and 4 retracing.

concepts.name: Motive Wave
concepts.blurb: A motive wave is Elliott Wave theory's trend engine: a five-wave structure, labeled 1 through 5, that moves in the direction of the trend one degree larger.

concepts.name: NeoWave Logic
concepts.blurb: NeoWave is Glenn Neely's reformulation of Elliott wave analysis, presented in his book Mastering Elliott Wave (1990).

concepts.name: Potential Reversal Zone
concepts.blurb: A Potential Reversal Zone (PRZ) is the completion window of a harmonic pattern: the price span where several separate Fibonacci measurements converge on the pattern's D point.

concepts.name: PRZ Execution
aliases: type I vs type II reversals
concepts.blurb: PRZ execution is the trade-management layer of harmonic trading: the set of techniques, largely codified by Scott Carney, for handling price once it actually enters a potential reversal zone.

concepts.name: RSI BAMM
concepts.blurb: RSI BAMM is Scott Carney's methodology for pairing a structural reading of the RSI with a harmonic price completion, extending his earlier BAMM concept from pure price geometry into momentum.

concepts.name: Shark

concepts.name: Three Drives
concepts.blurb: The Three Drives is a harmonic exhaustion pattern: three successive, symmetrical pushes to new extremes, each separated by a corrective pullback of similar depth.

concepts.name: Triangle
concepts.blurb: In Elliott wave analysis, a triangle is a five-legged sideways corrective structure, labeled A-B-C-D-E, in which every leg subdivides into three waves.

concepts.name: Truncation
concepts.blurb: Truncation, often called a failed fifth, occurs when the fifth wave of an impulse fails to exceed the extreme of the third wave.

concepts.name: Wave Degree Hierarchy
concepts.blurb: The wave degree hierarchy is the system of nested scales in Elliott wave theory: every wave is simultaneously a complete structure at its own degree and a component of a larger wave one degree higher.

concepts.name: Wave Extension

concepts.name: Zigzag

concepts.name: Abandoned Baby

concepts.name: Ascending Base
concepts.blurb: An ascending base is a growth-stock consolidation from the base taxonomy developed by William O'Neil and Investor's Business Daily.

concepts.name: Ascending/descending/symmetrical Triangle
concepts.blurb: Triangles are consolidations bounded by converging lines.

concepts.name: Bart Pattern
concepts.blurb: A Bart pattern is an informal crypto-chart formation named after the silhouette of Bart Simpson's head: a near-vertical rally, a flat sideways shelf, then a near-vertical drop that returns price…

concepts.name: Belt Hold

concepts.name: Breakaway Gap
concepts.blurb: A breakaway gap is the gap that starts a move.

concepts.name: Breakout Confirmation
concepts.blurb: Breakout confirmation is any rule that tries to separate a tradable break from a head-fake before full commitment.

concepts.name: Broadening Formation
concepts.blurb: A broadening formation, the megaphone, is a pattern of expanding swings: successive higher highs and lower lows contained by two diverging trendlines.

concepts.name: Bull/bear Flag
concepts.blurb: A flag is a brief continuation pattern: a sharp, near-vertical impulse leg (the pole), then a shallow countertrend drift inside a narrow parallel channel (the flag), then a break back in the pole's…

concepts.name: Bullish/bearish Engulfing
concepts.blurb: A bullish engulfing is a two-candle reversal pattern that appears after a decline.

concepts.name: Bump-and-run Reversal
concepts.blurb: The bump-and-run reversal is a chart pattern that describes the end of an unsustainable acceleration.

concepts.name: Candlestick Patterns
concepts.blurb: Candlestick patterns are recurring formations of one to five candles that traders read as shorthand for the shifting balance between buyers and sellers.

concepts.name: Channel Continuation
concepts.blurb: Channel continuation is the reading of a sloped parallel channel as a pause in a larger trend rather than a trend of its own.

concepts.name: Classic Bar Setups
concepts.blurb: Classic bar setups are the named one- and two-bar entries of late twentieth-century trading literature: patterns like Larry Williams' Oops, Joe Ross' gimmee bar, and 80-20 style reversal bars.

concepts.name: Common Gap
concepts.blurb: A common gap (also called an area or pattern gap) is the unremarkable member of the classical gap taxonomy: it opens inside an established trading range or a still-forming pattern, on unexceptional…

concepts.name: Complex H&S
concepts.blurb: A complex head and shoulders is a head and shoulders reversal with extra parts: two or more left shoulders, two or more right shoulders, or occasionally a double head.

concepts.name: Cup & Handle
concepts.blurb: A cup and handle is a bullish continuation pattern popularized by William J. O'Neil, the founder of Investor's Business Daily, in his 1988 book How to Make Money in Stocks.

concepts.name: Cup-with-handle Base
concepts.blurb: The cup-with-handle base is the flagship pattern of William O'Neil's growth-stock methodology, described in How to Make Money in Stocks.

concepts.name: Dark Cloud Cover
concepts.blurb: Dark cloud cover is a two-candle bearish reversal pattern from Japanese candlestick charting, introduced to Western readers by Steve Nison.

concepts.name: Diamond Top/bottom

concepts.name: Doji
concepts.blurb: A doji is a candlestick whose open and close land at, or almost at, the same price, collapsing the real body to a thin line while the shadows record the session's full travel.

concepts.name: Double-bottom Base
concepts.blurb: The double-bottom base is the W-shaped member of William O'Neil's base taxonomy: a growth stock corrects, rallies, then sells off again to a second low that undercuts the first before recovering and…

concepts.name: Double Top/bottom
concepts.blurb: A double top is two swing highs at about the same level with a pullback between them; a double bottom is the mirror image at the lows.

concepts.name: Dragonfly Doji
concepts.blurb: The dragonfly doji is a single candle shaped like a capital T: open, close, and high all sit at or very near the same price at the top of the range, with a long lower shadow beneath.

concepts.name: Engulfing Bar

concepts.name: Evening Star
concepts.blurb: An evening star is a three-candle bearish reversal pattern from Japanese candlestick analysis.

concepts.name: Exhaustion Bar
