concepts.name: Exhaustion Gap
concepts.blurb: An exhaustion gap is a price gap that appears late in an extended trend and marks its final push rather than its continuation.

concepts.name: Flat Base
concepts.blurb: A flat base is the quietest structure in William O'Neil's base taxonomy: a growth stock that has already advanced simply moves sideways in a tight range instead of correcting deeply.

concepts.name: Gap-and-go
concepts.blurb: Gap-and-go is a momentum day-trading setup built on an opening gap that refuses to fill.

concepts.name: Gap Fill
concepts.blurb: A gap fill is the return trip.

concepts.name: Gravestone Doji
concepts.blurb: The gravestone doji is a single candle shaped like an inverted T: open, close, and low all sit at or very near the same price at the bottom of the range, with a long upper shadow above.

concepts.name: Hammer
concepts.blurb: A hammer is a single-candle bullish reversal pattern from Japanese candlestick analysis.

concepts.name: Hanging Man
concepts.blurb: The hanging man is a single-candle bearish alert that appears after an advance: a small real body near the top of the range, a long lower shadow at least about twice the body's height, and little or…

concepts.name: Harami
concepts.blurb: A harami is a two-candle candlestick pattern in which the second candle's real body sits entirely inside the first candle's real body: a wide-range candle followed by a small one that fails to extend…

concepts.name: Head & Shoulders
concepts.blurb: A head and shoulders is the classic three-peak reversal pattern of Western charting, codified in the Schabacker and Edwards & Magee lineage.

concepts.name: High Tight Flag
concepts.blurb: The high tight flag is the most demanding continuation pattern in the growth-stock playbook: a stock roughly doubles in about two months or less, then pauses in a shallow, tight drift, typically…

concepts.name: High-wave Candle
concepts.blurb: A high-wave candle is a single candle with unusually long shadows on both sides and a small real body near the middle of the range.

concepts.name: Hikkake
concepts.blurb: A hikkake is an inside-bar false breakout, described by technician Daniel Chesler in the early 2000s; the name is Japanese for 'trap'.

concepts.name: Inside Bar
concepts.blurb: An inside bar is a bar whose entire range sits within the range of the bar before it: a lower high and a higher low than the preceding 'mother bar'.

concepts.name: Inverse Head & Shoulders
concepts.blurb: The inverse head and shoulders is the bottoming mirror of the head and shoulders top: three troughs, with the middle trough (the head) lower than the two flanking it (the shoulders), and a neckline…

concepts.name: Inverted Hammer
concepts.blurb: An inverted hammer is a single-candle bottom-reversal candidate: after a decline, a bar with a small real body at the lower end of its range, an upper shadow commonly at least twice the body's…

concepts.name: IPO Base
concepts.blurb: An IPO base is the first consolidation a newly listed stock forms after its market debut, a pattern named in William O'Neil's base taxonomy.

concepts.name: Island Reversal
concepts.blurb: An island reversal, sometimes called an island gap pair, is a compact group of price bars isolated from the surrounding trend by two gaps in opposite directions.

concepts.name: Key Reversal
concepts.blurb: A key reversal is a single-bar failure at a trend extreme.

concepts.name: Kicking
concepts.blurb: The kicking pattern, widely called a kicker in Western usage, is a two-candle reversal formation built from opposite-colored marubozu separated by a gap.

concepts.name: Marubozu
concepts.blurb: A marubozu is a candlestick that is all body: open and close sit at (or nearly at) the bar's extremes, leaving no meaningful shadow on either end.

concepts.name: Matching Low/high
concepts.blurb: The matching low is a two-candle pattern from the Japanese candlestick catalog.

concepts.name: Mat Hold
concepts.blurb: The mat hold is a five-candle continuation pattern from the Japanese candlestick catalog, and one of its rarer entries.

concepts.name: Measured-move Up/down
concepts.blurb: The measured-move up and its bearish mirror, the measured-move down, are three-part chart patterns: an initial trending leg, a corrective phase, and a second leg expected to roughly equal the first…

concepts.name: Measure Rule
concepts.blurb: The measure rule is the charting convention that a pattern projects a price objective equal to its own height.

concepts.name: Morning Star
concepts.blurb: A morning star is a three-candle bullish reversal pattern from Japanese candlestick tradition, printed at the bottom of a decline: a long bearish candle, then a small-bodied star that ideally gaps…

concepts.name: O'Neil Base Analysis
concepts.blurb: O'Neil base analysis is the chart-reading half of William O'Neil's growth-stock methodology, developed from his historical studies of leading stocks and taught through Investor's Business Daily and…

concepts.name: On-neck / In-neck / Thrusting
concepts.blurb: On-neck, in-neck, and thrusting are three closely related two-candle patterns from the Japanese candlestick catalog, all describing weak rallies inside a downtrend.

concepts.name: Outside Bar
concepts.blurb: An outside bar posts both a higher high and a lower low than the bar before it: its range fully engulfs the prior bar's range.

concepts.name: Pattern Failure Statistics
concepts.blurb: Pattern failure statistics are measured base rates for how often a chart pattern actually does what the textbook says.

concepts.name: Pennant
concepts.blurb: A pennant is a brief continuation pattern: a sharp, near-vertical move (the pole) followed by a small consolidation whose boundaries converge, forming a compact triangle that slopes gently against…

concepts.name: Piercing Line
concepts.blurb: A piercing line is a two-candle bullish reversal pattern from the Japanese candlestick catalog.

concepts.name: Pin Bar
concepts.blurb: A pin bar is a single bar with a long tail on one side and a small real body pushed toward the opposite end of the range.

concepts.name: Rare Candlestick Formations
concepts.blurb: Rare candlestick formations are the long tail of the Japanese candlestick catalog: patterns like the advance block, deliberation, three stars in the south, unique three-river bottom, concealing baby…

concepts.name: Rare Reversal Patterns
concepts.blurb: Rare reversal patterns are the low-frequency turning-point formations cataloged in Thomas Bulkowski's chart-pattern research and the Japanese candlestick literature: pipe tops and bottoms, horn tops…

concepts.name: Rectangle
concepts.blurb: A rectangle is a consolidation bounded by two roughly horizontal, parallel lines: price oscillates between a flat ceiling and a flat floor, with classical convention asking for at least two touches…

concepts.name: Rising/falling Three Methods
concepts.blurb: The rising three methods is a five-candle continuation pattern from the Japanese candlestick catalog.

concepts.name: Rising/falling Wedge
concepts.blurb: A wedge is a consolidation bounded by two converging trendlines that slope in the same direction.

concepts.name: Rounding Top/bottom
concepts.blurb: A rounding bottom, or saucer, is a gradual bowl-shaped reversal: a downtrend loses slope, the lows flatten, and higher lows build until price exits the basin on the upside.

concepts.name: Runaway Gap
concepts.blurb: A runaway gap, also called a measuring gap or continuation gap, is a price gap that appears in the middle of an established trend rather than at its beginning or end.

concepts.name: Scallop
concepts.blurb: A scallop is a curved continuation pattern shaped like the letter J or its mirror.

concepts.name: Shooting Star
concepts.blurb: A shooting star is a single-candle bearish reversal signal from the candlestick catalog: after an advance, a candle prints with a small real body near the session's low, a long upper shadow (commonly…

concepts.name: Spinning Top
concepts.blurb: A spinning top is a single candle with a small real body near the middle of its range and upper and lower shadows that are each longer than the body.

concepts.name: Three-bar Reversal
concepts.blurb: A three-bar reversal is the smallest complete turn a chart can print.

concepts.name: Three Black Crows
concepts.blurb: Three black crows is a three-candle bearish reversal pattern from the Japanese candlestick catalog.

concepts.name: Three Inside Up/down
concepts.blurb: Three inside up and three inside down are three-candle reversal patterns built directly on the harami.

concepts.name: Three Outside Up/down
concepts.blurb: Three outside up and three outside down are three-candle reversal patterns built on the engulfing pattern.

concepts.name: Three White Soldiers
concepts.blurb: Three white soldiers is a three-candle bullish reversal pattern from the Japanese candlestick catalog.

concepts.name: Triple Top/bottom
concepts.blurb: A triple top is a reversal pattern of three distinct peaks at roughly the same level, separated by two reactions, completed when price breaks below the lowest point between the peaks.

concepts.name: Tri-star
concepts.blurb: The tri-star is a rare three-candle reversal pattern from the Japanese candlestick tradition: three consecutive doji in which the middle doji gaps away from its neighbors.

concepts.name: Tweezer Top/bottom
concepts.blurb: Tweezers are two-candle reversal patterns in which consecutive candles print matching extremes: a tweezer top puts two highs at essentially the same price after an advance, and a tweezer bottom puts…

concepts.name: Two-bar Reversal
concepts.blurb: A two-bar reversal is a pair of consecutive, comparably strong bars that close at opposite ends of their ranges.

concepts.name: Upside/downside Tasuki Gap
concepts.blurb: The tasuki gap is a three-candle continuation pattern from Japanese candlestick analysis.

concepts.name: Volume Signature per Pattern
concepts.blurb: Volume signature per pattern is the classical-charting idea that every chart pattern has an expected volume shape, and that the pattern is only textbook when volume cooperates.

concepts.name: V-top/V-bottom
concepts.blurb: A V-top is a reversal with no top-building phase at all: a steep advance ends abruptly and turns into a steep decline, leaving a single sharp apex on the chart.

concepts.name: Weekend Gap
concepts.blurb: A weekend gap is the difference between where a market closes before the weekend and where it reopens after it.

concepts.name: Wide-range Bar
concepts.blurb: A wide-range bar (WRB) is a bar whose high-to-low span is unusually large for its context.

concepts.name: Wolfe Waves
concepts.blurb: Wolfe Waves are a five-point reversal pattern developed by Bill Wolfe, built from swing points labeled 1 through 5 inside a converging channel.

concepts.name: All-time & 52-week Extremes
concepts.blurb: All-time and 52-week extremes are the outer edges of an instrument's price history: the all-time high (ATH) and all-time low are the most extreme prices ever traded, and the 52-week high and low are…

concepts.name: Anchored VWAP As Level
concepts.blurb: Anchored VWAP as level is the practice of trading an anchored VWAP, the volume-weighted average price measured from a chosen event forward, as support and resistance in its own right.

concepts.name: Camarilla
concepts.blurb: Camarilla is a pivot framework that converts the prior session's range into a ladder of intraday support and resistance levels arranged around yesterday's close.

concepts.name: Central Pivot Range
concepts.blurb: The central pivot range (CPR) is a three-line pivot construct computed from the prior period's high, low, and close.

concepts.name: Curve Position
concepts.blurb: Curve position is how supply-and-demand traders answer the question of where price sits in the bigger picture.

concepts.name: DiNapoli Levels
concepts.blurb: DiNapoli levels are a disciplined application of Fibonacci analysis developed by trader Joe DiNapoli and set out in his book Trading with DiNapoli Levels.

concepts.name: Fib Clusters
concepts.blurb: Fib clusters are price zones where several independent Fibonacci measurements land on top of each other: a retracement of one swing, an extension of another, a projection from a third, often taken…

concepts.name: Fib Extension
concepts.blurb: A fib extension projects Fibonacci-ratio levels beyond the end of a measured swing.

concepts.name: Fib Geometry Tools
concepts.blurb: Fib geometry tools are the family of Fibonacci drawings that project ratio relationships as geometry instead of horizontal lines: fans (sloped rays), arcs and circles (curves at ratio-scaled radii),…

concepts.name: Fibonacci Pivots
concepts.blurb: Fibonacci pivots are a pivot-point family that spaces support and resistance at Fibonacci ratios of the prior period's range.

concepts.name: Fib Projection
concepts.blurb: A Fib projection is a three-point Fibonacci tool: it measures one completed swing, then plots ratios of that swing's length from a different starting point.

concepts.name: Fib Retracement
concepts.blurb: A Fib retracement maps horizontal levels across a completed price leg at fixed fractions of its range, conventionally 23.6%, 38.2%, 50%, 61.8%, and 78.6%.

concepts.name: Fib Time Tools
concepts.blurb: Fib time tools apply Fibonacci analysis to the horizontal axis of the chart instead of the vertical one.

concepts.name: Floor Pivots
concepts.blurb: Floor pivots, also called classic or traditional pivot points, are a ladder of intraday reference levels computed from the high, low, and close of the prior period.

concepts.name: Gann Square-of-9 Levels
concepts.blurb: Gann Square-of-9 levels are horizontal support and resistance prices projected from W.D. Gann's Square of 9, a spiral of integers winding outward from 1 so that each full loop returns to the same…

concepts.name: Golden Pocket
concepts.blurb: The golden pocket is the zone between the 0.618 and 0.65 levels of a Fibonacci retracement.

concepts.name: Level Clustering Algorithms
concepts.blurb: Level clustering algorithms turn a chart's scattered price extremes into a short, ranked list of support and resistance levels.

concepts.name: Level Freshness & Decay
concepts.blurb: Level freshness and decay is the idea that a level's expected behavior changes with every interaction.

concepts.name: Level Interaction Rules
concepts.blurb: Level interaction rules are the criteria that classify what price actually did at a level. 'Price came to support' is not an event; a wick through that closes back above, a full-bodied close below,…

concepts.name: Max Pain Level
concepts.blurb: The max pain level is the strike price at which the total payout to option holders at expiration would be smallest, computed from current open interest across all listed strikes.

concepts.name: Monday Range
concepts.blurb: The Monday range is the high and low of Monday's trading, held on the chart as a reference frame for the rest of the week.

concepts.name: Murrey Math Levels
concepts.blurb: Murrey Math levels are an algorithmic grid of nine horizontal lines, 0/8 through 8/8, dividing a reference frame of price into eighths, with overshoot lines at +1/8 and +2/8 above and -1/8 and -2/8…

concepts.name: Naked POC As Level
concepts.blurb: A naked POC, also called an untested or virgin point of control, is the point of control of a completed session or profile that price has never revisited since that session ended.

concepts.name: Option Strike Walls
concepts.blurb: Option strike walls are levels on the underlying's chart derived from the options market: strikes where unusually large open interest, volume, or estimated dealer gamma exposure is concentrated.

concepts.name: Overnight & ETH Levels
concepts.blurb: Overnight and ETH levels are reference prices formed outside the regular session: the overnight high and low (ONH/ONL) built during a futures contract's extended electronic hours, and the pre-market…

concepts.name: Period Opens
concepts.blurb: Period opens are the opening prices of calendar periods, the day, week, month, quarter, and year, plotted as horizontal levels on lower-timeframe charts.

concepts.name: Pivot Points
concepts.blurb: Pivot points are formula-derived support and resistance levels computed from the prior period's price data (usually the high, low, and close) and projected onto the current session before it opens.

concepts.name: Prior Period Levels
concepts.blurb: Prior period levels are the high, low, and close of a completed period, the previous day, week, month, quarter, or year, projected forward onto the current chart as horizontal references.

concepts.name: Resistance Level
concepts.blurb: A resistance level is a price area above the current market where advances have repeatedly stalled or reversed.

concepts.name: Role Reversal
concepts.blurb: Role reversal, also called the polarity principle or the S/R flip, is the classical rule that a broken support level tends to act as resistance once price trades below it, and broken resistance tends…

concepts.name: Round Numbers
concepts.blurb: Round numbers, often called psychological levels, are prices ending in zeros or clean fractions: 1.1000 in FX (a big figure, with the double-zero 00 levels and the 25/50/75 quarter grid between…

concepts.name: S/R Zone
concepts.blurb: An S/R zone is support or resistance drawn as a band rather than a single line.

concepts.name: Supply & Demand Zones
concepts.blurb: Supply and demand zones mark the origins of imbalanced moves.

concepts.name: Support Level
concepts.blurb: A support level is a price where a market has repeatedly stopped falling and turned higher, drawn as a horizontal line beneath current price.

concepts.name: Tirone Levels
concepts.blurb: Tirone levels are horizontal support and resistance lines derived from the highest high and lowest low of a chosen lookback window, attributed to analyst John Tirone.

concepts.name: Woodie Pivots
concepts.blurb: Woodie pivots are a variant of the classic pivot-point set, named for the trader Ken Wood (Woodie), that changes the weighting of the central pivot.

concepts.name: Zone Scoring & Refinement
concepts.blurb: Zone scoring and refinement is the rule set supply-and-demand traders use to grade a supply or demand zone before trusting it.

concepts.name: Adaptive-parameter Technique
concepts.blurb: An adaptive-parameter technique replaces a fixed indicator setting, such as a 14-bar lookback or a smoothing constant, with a value computed from the market itself.

concepts.name: Alpha
concepts.blurb: Alpha is the part of an asset's or strategy's return that its market exposure does not explain.

concepts.name: Autocorrelation
concepts.blurb: Autocorrelation is the correlation of a series with a lagged copy of itself.

concepts.name: Autocorrelation Periodogram
concepts.blurb: The autocorrelation periodogram is John Ehlers' spectral estimator for finding the dominant cycle in price.

concepts.name: Beta
concepts.blurb: Beta measures how strongly an asset's returns move with a benchmark's.

concepts.name: Change-point Detection
concepts.blurb: Change-point detection is the statistical problem of locating when a time series' generating process shifted: a change in mean, in variance, or in distribution, as opposed to where price is heading…

concepts.name: Cointegration
concepts.blurb: Cointegration is a long-run statistical tether between price series.

concepts.name: Correlation
concepts.blurb: Correlation measures how consistently two series move together, on a scale from -1 to +1.

concepts.name: Decycler
concepts.blurb: The decycler is a smoothing filter introduced by John Ehlers in Cycle Analytics for Traders (2013).

concepts.name: Distribution Moments
concepts.blurb: Distribution moments are the statistics that summarize the shape of a return distribution.

concepts.name: Distribution-of-returns Profiling
concepts.blurb: Distribution-of-returns profiling builds the empirical distribution of a market's moves from history and reads its shape directly, instead of assuming a bell curve.

concepts.name: Dominant Cycle Measurement
concepts.blurb: Dominant cycle measurement is a family of signal-processing techniques, developed for trading largely by John Ehlers, that estimate the period of the strongest cycle currently present in price.

concepts.name: Entropy Measures
concepts.blurb: Entropy measures quantify how disordered or unpredictable a series is.

concepts.name: Even-better Sinewave
concepts.blurb: The even-better sinewave is a John Ehlers indicator, published in Cycle Analytics for Traders (2013) as an improvement on his earlier sinewave indicator.

concepts.name: Exponential Smoothing Forecasts
concepts.blurb: Exponential smoothing forecasts extrapolate a series from exponentially weighted averages of its own past, with recent data counting most.

concepts.name: FFT/spectral Analysis
concepts.blurb: Spectral analysis asks how much of a series' variance lives at each frequency.

concepts.name: Fractal Dimension
concepts.blurb: Fractal dimension measures how rough a curve is, or equivalently how much space it fills.

concepts.name: Hilbert Transform
concepts.blurb: The Hilbert transform is a signal-processing operation that shifts every frequency component of a series by 90 degrees.

concepts.name: Hodrick-Prescott Filter
concepts.blurb: The Hodrick-Prescott (HP) filter is a trend-extraction method from macroeconometrics, introduced to economics by Robert Hodrick and Edward Prescott for separating business-cycle fluctuations from…

concepts.name: Hurst Exponent
concepts.blurb: The Hurst exponent (H) measures long-range dependence in a series: whether moves tend to continue, partially reverse, or wander at random.

concepts.name: Kalman Filter
concepts.blurb: A Kalman filter is a recursive estimator, introduced by Rudolf Kálmán in 1960 for control engineering, that tracks the hidden state of a noisy system one observation at a time.

concepts.name: Lead-lag Detection
concepts.blurb: Lead-lag detection asks whether one instrument's moves systematically precede another's.

concepts.name: Linear Regression
concepts.blurb: Linear regression fits a straight line through the last N bars of price by ordinary least squares.

concepts.name: LOESS Smoothing
concepts.blurb: LOESS (locally estimated scatterplot smoothing) fits a smooth curve through noisy data one point at a time.

concepts.name: Market Efficiency & Regime Persistence Measures
concepts.blurb: Market efficiency and regime persistence measures are statistics that score how directionally efficient price travel is and how long directional regimes tend to last.

concepts.name: Maximum-entropy Spectrum
concepts.blurb: Maximum-entropy spectral analysis, widely known by the acronym MESA, is a method for estimating which cycle periods are present in a data series.

concepts.name: Min-max Scaling
concepts.blurb: Min-max scaling rescales a series to a fixed interval, usually 0 to 1 or 0 to 100, by subtracting the window minimum and dividing by the window range (maximum minus minimum).

concepts.name: Monte Carlo Price Paths
concepts.blurb: Monte Carlo price paths are simulated futures: many hypothetical forward trajectories generated by drawing random per-bar returns and compounding them from the current price.

concepts.name: Normality Testing
concepts.blurb: Normality testing asks a blunt statistical question of a return series: is it plausible that these observations came from a normal (Gaussian) distribution?

concepts.name: Outlier Detection
concepts.blurb: Outlier detection flags observations that sit far outside the typical run of a series: a return, a volume print, or an indicator value that does not belong to the recent distribution.

concepts.name: Pairs Trading Stack
concepts.blurb: The pairs trading stack is the chain of statistical steps that turns two related instruments into one tradable spread.

concepts.name: Percentile Rank
concepts.blurb: Percentile rank locates the current value of a series within its own recent history: it is the percentage of values in a lookback window that sit at or below the current one.

concepts.name: Polynomial Regression
concepts.blurb: Polynomial regression fits a curved line to price by least squares: instead of a straight linear regression, the model adds squared, cubed, and higher powers of the bar index, then solves for the…

concepts.name: Probability Cones
concepts.blurb: Probability cones are forward-projected envelopes, anchored at the current price, an entry, or an event, that show where price is statistically expected to remain at chosen confidence levels.

concepts.name: Quantile Regression
concepts.blurb: Quantile regression fits a line to a chosen quantile of the data instead of its mean.

concepts.name: Random-entry Baselines
concepts.blurb: A random-entry baseline is a control experiment for a trading system: replace the system's entry signal with a coin flip, keep everything else identical (the exits, the position sizing, the…

concepts.name: Resampling Tests
concepts.blurb: Resampling tests estimate uncertainty by redrawing from the data you already have instead of assuming a theoretical distribution.

concepts.name: Roofing Filter
concepts.blurb: A roofing filter is John Ehlers' preprocessing bandpass for indicator inputs.

concepts.name: Sigmoid/softmax Transforms
concepts.blurb: Sigmoid transforms are S-shaped functions that squash an unbounded input into a fixed interval.

concepts.name: Signal Decomposition
concepts.blurb: Signal decomposition splits a price series into additive components, typically a slow trend, one or more oscillatory parts, and residual noise, so each can be analyzed or traded on its own.

concepts.name: Sinewave Indicator
concepts.blurb: The Sinewave Indicator is John Ehlers' cycle-timing tool.

concepts.name: Standard Deviation
concepts.blurb: Standard deviation, often abbreviated stdev and written with the Greek letter sigma, is the classic statistical measure of dispersion: the square root of the average squared distance between each…

concepts.name: Stationarity & Efficiency Tests
concepts.blurb: Stationarity and efficiency tests ask two related questions of a series: do its statistical properties (mean, variance) stay stable through time, and does the series follow a random walk, with…

concepts.name: Wavelet Decomposition
concepts.blurb: Wavelet decomposition splits a time series into components at different scales: a smooth approximation capturing the slow trend, plus layers of detail capturing progressively faster fluctuations.

concepts.name: Winsorization
concepts.blurb: Winsorization is a technique for limiting the influence of extreme values in a data set: instead of deleting outliers, every value beyond a chosen percentile is replaced with the value at that…

concepts.name: Z-score
concepts.blurb: A z-score expresses how far the current value of a series sits from its recent average, measured in standard deviations.

concepts.name: Bagging
concepts.blurb: Bagging, short for bootstrap aggregating, is an ensemble method that trains many copies of the same model on different bootstrap samples of the training data and averages their predictions (or takes…

concepts.name: Bayesian Classifiers
concepts.blurb: A Bayesian classifier assigns a probability to each possible outcome class, such as price up versus price down over the next several bars, by applying Bayes' theorem: the posterior probability of a…

concepts.name: Decision Trees
concepts.blurb: A decision tree predicts by asking a sequence of yes/no questions about the input features, such as whether RSI is below 30 or whether relative volume exceeds 1.5, and routing each observation down…

concepts.name: Dynamic Time Warping Similarity
concepts.blurb: Dynamic time warping (DTW) measures how similar two sequences are when they may unfold at different speeds.

concepts.name: Ensemble Voting of Signals
concepts.blurb: Ensemble voting of signals combines several independent signals or models into a single output by letting them vote.

concepts.name: Feature Engineering
concepts.blurb: Feature engineering is the step in a machine-learning pipeline where raw market data is turned into the input variables a model actually learns from.

concepts.name: Feature Selection
concepts.blurb: Feature selection is the process of choosing which candidate inputs a model is allowed to use and discarding the rest.

concepts.name: Gaussian Mixture Models
concepts.blurb: A Gaussian mixture model (GMM) assumes the observed data were drawn from a blend of several normal distributions, each with its own mean, variance (covariance in higher dimensions), and mixture…

concepts.name: Gaussian Process Regression
concepts.blurb: Gaussian process regression (GPR) is a Bayesian, nonparametric way to fit a smooth curve through data.

concepts.name: Gradient Boosting
concepts.blurb: Gradient boosting builds a strong model as a sum of many weak ones, usually shallow decision trees, added one at a time.

concepts.name: Hidden Markov / Markov-switching Regimes
concepts.blurb: Hidden Markov and Markov-switching models describe the market as moving between a small number of unobserved states, or regimes, such as quiet uptrend, volatile selloff, and rangebound chop.

concepts.name: Kernel Density Estimation
concepts.blurb: Kernel density estimation (KDE) is a nonparametric way to estimate a probability distribution from data without assuming its shape.

concepts.name: Kernel Regression
concepts.blurb: Kernel regression is a nonparametric way to draw a smooth curve through noisy data.

concepts.name: K-means Regime Clustering
concepts.blurb: K-means is an unsupervised algorithm that partitions observations into k groups.

concepts.name: kNN Analog Forecasting
concepts.blurb: kNN analog forecasting applies the k-nearest-neighbors method to price history.

concepts.name: Label Definition & Prediction Horizon
concepts.blurb: In supervised machine learning for trading, the label is the target the model learns to predict, and the prediction horizon is how far into the future that target looks.

concepts.name: LLM/transformer-derived Signals
concepts.blurb: LLM and transformer-derived signals are trading inputs produced by transformer models, the neural architecture behind large language models.

concepts.name: Logistic Signal Calibration
concepts.blurb: Logistic signal calibration is the use of logistic regression, or the logistic (sigmoid) function more generally, to turn indicator readings into a probability-style score between 0 and 1.

concepts.name: LSTM / Recurrent Networks
concepts.blurb: Recurrent networks are neural networks built for sequences: they process one step at a time while carrying a hidden state forward, so earlier bars influence how later bars are read.

concepts.name: Matrix Profile
concepts.blurb: The matrix profile is a data structure for time series that stores, for every subsequence of a chosen length, the distance to its nearest neighbor elsewhere in the same series (or in a second series).

concepts.name: Model Overfitting
concepts.blurb: Model overfitting occurs when a model learns the noise in its training data rather than the repeatable structure, so it scores well on the data it was fitted to and poorly on anything new.

concepts.name: Model Stacking
concepts.blurb: Model stacking, also called stacked generalization, combines several predictive models by training a second-level model on their outputs.

concepts.name: Neural Networks
concepts.blurb: A neural network is a function approximator built from layers of simple units.

concepts.name: Online/incremental Learning
concepts.blurb: Online, or incremental, learning updates a model continuously as new data arrives instead of refitting it on a stored batch.

concepts.name: PCA
concepts.blurb: Principal component analysis (PCA) re-expresses a set of correlated variables as a smaller set of uncorrelated ones.

concepts.name: Probability Calibration Curves
concepts.blurb: A probability calibration curve, often called a reliability diagram, tests whether a model's stated probabilities mean what they say.

concepts.name: Random Forest
concepts.blurb: A random forest is an ensemble model that trains many decision trees and combines them, by majority vote for classification or by averaging for regression.

concepts.name: Reinforcement-learning Policies
concepts.blurb: Reinforcement learning (RL) frames trading as sequential decision-making.

concepts.name: Self-organizing Maps

concepts.name: Spectral Clustering
concepts.blurb: This is a graph-based grouping technique: instead of partitioning data points by their raw distance from center points, it first builds a similarity graph, where each observation is a node and edge…

concepts.name: Support Vector Machines
concepts.blurb: A support vector machine (SVM) is a supervised classifier that separates two classes with the boundary maximizing the margin, the distance to the nearest training points on each side.

concepts.name: Train/validation Discipline
concepts.blurb: Train/validation discipline is the set of rules governing which data a model may learn from and which data may judge it.

concepts.name: Asset-class Seasonality
concepts.blurb: Asset-class seasonality is the observation that calendar patterns differ fundamentally across asset types because the drivers differ.

concepts.name: Astro Cycles
concepts.blurb: Astro cycles is the umbrella term for market-timing methods based on astronomical or astrological calendars: lunar cycles (new and full moons), planetary aspects and alignments, eclipses, and…

concepts.name: Auction Windows
concepts.blurb: Auction windows are the scheduled periods around the official opening and closing auctions of exchange-listed markets, when exchanges batch orders and match them at a single price.

concepts.name: Buyback Blackout Windows
concepts.blurb: Buyback blackout windows are the recurring periods around earnings releases when companies voluntarily suspend discretionary repurchases of their own stock.

concepts.name: Crypto Halving Cycle
concepts.blurb: The crypto halving cycle is the roughly four-year rhythm in Bitcoin's price history anchored to its halvings: protocol-scheduled events every 210,000 blocks that cut the new-coin reward paid to…

concepts.name: Day-of-week Effects
concepts.blurb: Day-of-week effects are calendar tendencies in which average return, volatility, or volume differs by weekday.

concepts.name: Defining Range
concepts.blurb: A defining range (DR) is a fixed one-hour window whose extremes become the reference frame for the rest of a trading session.

concepts.name: Delta Phenomenon
concepts.blurb: The Delta Phenomenon is a market-timing theory published by J. Welles Wilder Jr. in 1991, based on an idea he credited to trader Jim Sloman.

concepts.name: Dominant-cycle Detection
concepts.blurb: Dominant-cycle detection is the attempt to identify, bar by bar, the period of the strongest cyclical component currently present in price.

concepts.name: Expiration Effects
concepts.blurb: Expiration effects are the recurring price and volume behaviors that surround the scheduled expiration of derivatives.

concepts.name: Fixed Time Cycles
concepts.blurb: Fixed time cycles model a market as repeating a rhythm of constant length: a low or a turn every N bars, days, or weeks, projected forward from a chosen anchor.

concepts.name: Futures Roll Dates
concepts.blurb: Futures roll dates are the periods when trading activity migrates from an expiring futures contract to the next one out on the curve.

concepts.name: Gann Time Cycles/anniversaries
concepts.blurb: Gann time cycles and anniversaries are the time-based side of W.D. Gann's methodology: projecting future turning-point dates from the dates of past major highs and lows.

concepts.name: Gap Rules Interaction
concepts.blurb: Gap rules interaction is the practice of reading an opening gap together with the session's opening-range levels and the prior day's reference levels, rather than in isolation.

concepts.name: Hurst Cycle Analysis
concepts.blurb: Hurst cycle analysis is the framework developed by J.M. Hurst, an American aerospace engineer, in 'The Profit Magic of Stock Transaction Timing' (1970) and his later Cycles Course.

concepts.name: Intraday Time-of-day Effects
concepts.blurb: Intraday time-of-day effects are the repeatable patterns that volume, volatility, and liquidity trace across the trading day.

concepts.name: January Effect
concepts.blurb: The January effect is the historical tendency of stocks, especially small-caps, to post unusually strong returns in January, documented in US academic studies of the 1970s and 1980s.

concepts.name: Long-horizon Calendar Cycles
concepts.blurb: Long-horizon calendar cycles are multi-year market rhythms anchored to the calendar itself rather than measured from price.

concepts.name: Macro Event Days
concepts.blurb: Macro event days are sessions dominated by scheduled economic releases: central-bank decisions and press conferences (FOMC, ECB), inflation prints like CPI, US nonfarm payrolls, and similar red-flag…

concepts.name: Month-of-year Seasonality
concepts.blurb: Month-of-year seasonality is the tendency for average returns to differ by calendar month, measured by laying years of monthly returns into a matrix (years down the rows, months across the columns)…

concepts.name: Opening Range & ORB
concepts.blurb: The opening range is the high-low span a market prints in the first minutes of a session, most commonly the first 5, 15, 30, or 60 minutes after the open.

concepts.name: Pre-holiday Drift
concepts.blurb: Pre-holiday drift is the historical tendency of equity markets to post above-average returns on the trading day (or days) immediately before exchange holidays.

concepts.name: Quarterly Earnings Season Phases
concepts.blurb: Earnings season is the several-week stretch after each calendar quarter when most listed US companies report results, beginning roughly two weeks into January, April, July, and October.

concepts.name: RTH vs ETH
concepts.blurb: RTH vs ETH is the split between Regular Trading Hours, the official cash session (9:30am to 4:00pm ET for US equities, with index futures' RTH conventionally aligned to it), and Extended or…

concepts.name: Santa Claus Rally
concepts.blurb: The Santa Claus rally is the tendency of US stocks to post small gains over a specific seven-session window: the last five trading days of December plus the first two trading days of January.

concepts.name: Seasonality Tooling
concepts.blurb: Seasonality tooling is the set of displays and statistics that make calendar tendencies inspectable: N-year average paths, return matrices and heat maps, and consistency scores.

concepts.name: sell-in-May
concepts.blurb: "Sell in May and go away" is the adage that equities earn most of their return from November through April and comparatively little from May through October.

concepts.name: Session High/low Statistics
concepts.blurb: Session high/low statistics measure when a session's extreme prices tend to form.

concepts.name: Session Open/close Behaviors
concepts.blurb: Session open/close behaviors are the recurring shifts in volatility and order flow around the boundaries of the major trading sessions.

concepts.name: Tax-loss Selling Season
concepts.blurb: Tax-loss selling season is the late-year stretch when investors sell losing positions to realize capital losses that offset taxable gains.

concepts.name: Trading Sessions
concepts.blurb: Trading sessions are the recurring daily windows when each major financial center is active: Sydney and Tokyo through the Asian hours, London through the European morning and afternoon, New York…

concepts.name: Turn-of-month Effects
concepts.blurb: Turn-of-month effects refer to the historical tendency of equity returns to concentrate in a narrow window around the month boundary, classically defined as the last trading day of the month through…

concepts.name: 0DTE Flow Effects
concepts.blurb: 0DTE options are contracts with zero days to expiration: they expire the same session they trade.

concepts.name: 13F Concentration
concepts.blurb: Form 13F is the quarterly disclosure the SEC requires from institutional investment managers overseeing at least $100 million in qualifying US securities.

concepts.name: Advance/decline Internals
concepts.blurb: Advance/decline internals are the breadth statistics built from two counts: how many issues on an exchange closed higher (advances) and how many closed lower (declines).

concepts.name: Alternative Sentiment Data
concepts.blurb: Alternative sentiment data is the umbrella term for crowd-mood measures built from sources outside the market itself: search interest from Google Trends, message volume and tone on X, Reddit, and…

concepts.name: Analyst Revision Breadth
concepts.blurb: Analyst revision breadth measures the balance between upward and downward changes in sell-side forecasts across a universe of stocks.

concepts.name: Breadth Omens
concepts.blurb: Breadth omens are composite warning signals built from market internals, the best known being the Hindenburg Omen and the Titanic Syndrome.

concepts.name: Breadth Thrusts
concepts.blurb: Breadth thrusts are rare, high-velocity swings in market breadth from washed-out to overwhelmingly positive, read as evidence that buying has broadened enough to start a durable advance.

concepts.name: Buyback Flows
concepts.blurb: Buyback flows are the aggregate demand created by companies repurchasing their own shares, typically through open-market programs run under the SEC's Rule 10b-18 safe harbor or pre-scheduled 10b5-1…

concepts.name: COT Analysis
concepts.blurb: COT analysis reads the Commitments of Traders reports the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission publishes each week: a snapshot of open futures positions (with a combined futures-and-options…

concepts.name: Credit Spreads
concepts.blurb: Credit spreads are the extra yield corporate bonds pay over comparable government bonds, compensation for bearing default and liquidity risk.

concepts.name: Crypto Cycle Models
concepts.blurb: Crypto cycle models are frameworks for estimating where Bitcoin, and by extension the wider crypto market, sits inside its multi-year boom and bust sequence, which has historically tracked the…

concepts.name: Currency Strength Meter
concepts.blurb: A currency strength meter scores each currency on its own by aggregating its performance across a basket of pairs.

concepts.name: Dark Pool Prints
concepts.blurb: Dark pool prints are trades executed on off-exchange venues, alternative trading systems that display no public order book, and then reported to the consolidated tape through FINRA's trade reporting…

concepts.name: DXY Correlation Regimes
concepts.blurb: DXY correlation regimes describe how the relationship between the U.S. Dollar Index and other markets shifts over time.

concepts.name: Equal-weight vs Cap-weight Ratio
concepts.blurb: The equal-weight vs cap-weight ratio divides an equal-weighted version of an index by its capitalization-weighted version, for example an equal-weight S&P 500 fund against the standard cap-weighted…

concepts.name: ES Fair-value Basis
concepts.blurb: The ES fair-value basis is the gap between the S&P 500 E-mini futures price and the contract's theoretical fair value implied by cost of carry.

concepts.name: Exchange & Stablecoin Flows
concepts.blurb: Exchange and stablecoin flows are on-chain supply metrics built from labeled exchange wallets.

concepts.name: Fear & Greed Index
concepts.blurb: The Fear & Greed Index is a composite sentiment gauge that compresses several market-based inputs into a single 0 to 100 reading, where low values label extreme fear and high values extreme greed.

concepts.name: Fund Flows
concepts.blurb: Fund flows measure the net money investors move into or out of pooled vehicles, chiefly mutual funds and ETFs.

concepts.name: Funding Rate
concepts.blurb: A funding rate is the periodic payment that keeps a perpetual futures contract tracking its underlying spot index.

concepts.name: Futures Basis
concepts.blurb: Futures basis is the gap between a derivative's price and the spot price of the same asset, quoted as a raw spread or annualized into a percentage yield.

concepts.name: Gamma Exposure
concepts.blurb: Gamma exposure (GEX) estimates how much option dealers' hedging must respond to price movement.

concepts.name: Implied Volatility
concepts.blurb: Implied volatility (IV) is the volatility number that makes an option-pricing model's theoretical price match the option's actual market price.

concepts.name: Insider Transactions
concepts.blurb: Insider transactions are trades in a company's own shares by its officers, directors, and owners of more than 10% of the stock.

concepts.name: Intermarket Analysis
concepts.blurb: Intermarket analysis is the practice of reading the four major asset classes (currencies, bonds, stocks, and commodities) as one linked system rather than in isolation.

concepts.name: Liquidation Clusters
concepts.blurb: Liquidation clusters are price zones where a large amount of leveraged derivative exposure would be force-closed if the market traded there.

concepts.name: Long/short Account Ratio
concepts.blurb: The long/short account ratio is an exchange-published positioning metric: among accounts holding an open position in a given perpetual or futures contract, the number net long divided by the number…

concepts.name: Macro Event Playbooks
concepts.blurb: Macro event playbooks are the prepared routines traders build around scheduled economic releases and central bank decisions: FOMC meetings, CPI, nonfarm payrolls, and the PMI/ISM survey cycle.

concepts.name: Magazine-cover Indicator
concepts.blurb: The magazine-cover indicator is market folklore holding that when a financial trend makes the cover of a mainstream, general-interest publication, that trend is close to exhaustion.

concepts.name: Margin Debt
concepts.blurb: Margin debt is the total amount investors have borrowed from brokers against their portfolios.

concepts.name: Max Pain
concepts.blurb: Max pain is the strike at which options expiring on a given date would pay out the least in total.

concepts.name: McClellan Oscillator
concepts.blurb: The McClellan Oscillator is a breadth-momentum indicator developed by Sherman and Marian McClellan in 1969, building on P.N. Haurlan's early use of exponential smoothing in market analysis.

concepts.name: MVRV
concepts.blurb: MVRV (Market Value to Realized Value) is an on-chain valuation ratio: a crypto asset's market capitalization divided by its realized capitalization.

concepts.name: New Highs − New Lows
concepts.blurb: New Highs − New Lows (net new highs) is a breadth measure: each day, count the stocks in an exchange or index making fresh 52-week highs, subtract those making fresh 52-week lows, and plot the result.

concepts.name: NVT Ratio
concepts.blurb: The NVT Ratio (Network Value to Transactions) divides a crypto asset's market capitalization by the value transacted on its blockchain each day, usually measured in dollars.

concepts.name: Odd-lot Activity
concepts.blurb: An odd lot is an order or trade smaller than the standard round lot, which has historically been 100 shares in US equities.

concepts.name: On-chain Valuation Suite
concepts.blurb: The on-chain valuation suite is the family of metrics that values a crypto asset from its own blockchain data rather than from price action alone.

concepts.name: Open Interest
concepts.blurb: Open interest is the total number of derivative contracts (futures, options, perpetual swaps) currently open: entered into and not yet closed, settled, or liquidated.

concepts.name: Participation Divergence at Index Highs
concepts.blurb: Participation divergence at index highs is the breadth analyst's core warning pattern: a cap-weighted index prints a new high while the measures of participation underneath it do not.

concepts.name: Power-law Growth Curves
concepts.blurb: Power-law growth curves model an asset's long-run price as a power function of time: price proportional to elapsed time (measured from some origin, such as Bitcoin's genesis block) raised to a fixed…

concepts.name: Put/call Ratio
concepts.blurb: The put/call ratio divides the volume of put options traded by the volume of call options traded over a session, either for a single underlying or aggregated across a whole market.

concepts.name: Ratio Charts
concepts.blurb: A ratio chart plots one instrument's price divided by another's, bar by bar, so the line rises when the numerator outperforms and falls when it underperforms.

concepts.name: Real Yields
concepts.blurb: Real yields are government bond yields adjusted for expected inflation: what lenders earn in purchasing-power terms.

concepts.name: Relative Rotation Graphs
concepts.blurb: A Relative Rotation Graph (RRG) is a two-axis scatter view of relative strength, created by Julius de Kempenaer.

concepts.name: Relative Strength Comparative
concepts.blurb: Relative strength comparative measures how an instrument performs against a benchmark or another instrument, most simply as the RS line: the stock's price divided by an index, plotted bar by bar.

concepts.name: Risk Reversals
concepts.blurb: A risk reversal is two things.

concepts.name: Sector Breadth
concepts.blurb: Sector breadth measures participation at the sector level rather than the single-stock or whole-index level.

concepts.name: Sector Rotation Model
concepts.blurb: A sector rotation model is a framework that reads market regime through which sectors are leading.

concepts.name: Sentiment Surveys
concepts.blurb: Sentiment surveys are recurring polls that ask a defined group of investors how they feel about the market, published as the share of respondents in each stance.

concepts.name: Short Interest
concepts.blurb: Short interest is the total number of shares sold short and not yet bought back.

concepts.name: SKEW Index
concepts.blurb: The Cboe SKEW Index measures how steeply the S&P 500 options market prices tail risk over roughly the next 30 days.

concepts.name: SOPR
concepts.blurb: SOPR (Spent Output Profit Ratio) is an on-chain Bitcoin metric introduced by Renato Shirakashi in 2019.

concepts.name: % Stocks Above 20/50/200-day MA
concepts.blurb: The percentage of stocks above a moving average is a diffusion index: score each constituent of an index or exchange 1 if it trades above its own N-day simple moving average and 0 if not, then…

concepts.name: Strike Walls
concepts.blurb: Strike walls are option strikes carrying unusually large open interest or dealer gamma for a given expiry.

concepts.name: TICK Index
concepts.blurb: The TICK index is a real-time market internal: at any moment it equals the number of NYSE stocks whose most recent trade printed on an uptick minus the number whose last trade printed on a downtick…

concepts.name: TRIN
concepts.blurb: TRIN, short for Trading Index and better known as the Arms Index after Richard Arms, who introduced it in 1967, is a market breadth ratio built from exchange internals.

concepts.name: Up/down Volume
concepts.blurb: Up/down volume is a breadth measure that splits a session's total exchange volume by direction: up volume is the combined volume of advancing issues, down volume the combined volume of decliners,…

concepts.name: Vanna/charm Flows
concepts.blurb: Vanna and charm are second-order option Greeks.

concepts.name: VIX
concepts.blurb: The VIX is Cboe's Volatility Index: a live estimate of how much volatility the options market expects from the S&P 500 over the next 30 days, expressed in annualized percentage points.

concepts.name: VIX Term Structure
concepts.blurb: The VIX term structure is the curve of expected S&P 500 volatility across time horizons, built from the spot VIX and the strip of VIX futures expiring in successive months.

concepts.name: VVIX
concepts.blurb: The VVIX is Cboe's volatility-of-volatility index.

concepts.name: Whale-wallet Tracking
concepts.blurb: Whale-wallet tracking is the practice of monitoring blockchain addresses that hold or move unusually large balances in order to infer what the biggest holders are doing.

concepts.name: Yield Curve
concepts.blurb: The yield curve is the line traced by government bond yields across maturities, from short-term bills out to long bonds.

concepts.name: Averaging Down
concepts.blurb: Averaging down is adding to a losing position at better prices: buying more as price falls (or selling more as it rises against a short) so the average entry improves.

concepts.name: Breakeven Move Rules
concepts.blurb: Breakeven move rules are trade-management rules that move the stop loss to the entry price once the trade has moved a predefined distance in favor, most commonly one initial risk unit, that is, at…

concepts.name: DCA
concepts.blurb: DCA, dollar-cost averaging, is buying a fixed cash amount of an asset on a fixed schedule regardless of price.

concepts.name: Elder SafeZone Stop
concepts.blurb: The SafeZone stop is Alexander Elder's noise-based trailing stop, introduced in his book Come Into My Trading Room (2002).

concepts.name: Equity-curve-based Throttling
concepts.blurb: Equity-curve-based throttling, often called trading the equity curve, treats a strategy's own profit-and-loss line as an input to risk decisions.

concepts.name: Exchange Order Flags
concepts.blurb: Exchange order flags are modifiers attached to an order that change how the matching engine is allowed to handle it, without changing the order's basic type.

concepts.name: Execution Cost Modeling
concepts.blurb: Execution cost modeling is the practice of estimating the gap between the prices a strategy assumes and the prices real orders achieve.

concepts.name: Fixed Fractional
concepts.blurb: Fixed fractional, also called percent-risk sizing, risks the same fraction of current equity on every trade.

concepts.name: Fixed Ratio
concepts.blurb: Fixed ratio is a position sizing method introduced by Ryan Jones in his book The Trading Game (1999).

concepts.name: Fixed Stops
concepts.blurb: Fixed stops are exits defined by a predetermined rule rather than by chart context: a set percentage or dollar distance from entry, a time stop that closes the trade after a set number of bars, or a…

concepts.name: Kelly Criterion
concepts.blurb: The Kelly criterion is a formula for the fraction of capital to commit to a favorable bet so that the long-run growth rate of the account is maximized.

concepts.name: Loss-control Rules
concepts.blurb: Loss-control rules are account-level circuit breakers: predefined conditions under which trading stops or shrinks for the rest of a session, day, or week.

concepts.name: MAE/MFE-informed Management
concepts.blurb: MAE/MFE-informed management is the practice of setting stops, targets, and trade-management rules from the measured excursion history of a strategy's own trades.

concepts.name: Martingale / Anti-martingale
concepts.blurb: Martingale and anti-martingale are the two opposite ways of coupling position size to recent results.

concepts.name: Max Heat
concepts.blurb: Max heat is a portfolio-level risk cap: the maximum total amount, expressed as a percentage of equity, that all open positions together are allowed to lose if every stop is hit at once.

concepts.name: Mental vs Hard Stop
concepts.blurb: A hard stop is a resting stop order held at the broker or exchange: if price touches the level, the position is closed mechanically, no decision required.

concepts.name: Non-price Exits
concepts.blurb: Non-price exits are rules that close a trade for reasons other than price reaching a predefined level.

concepts.name: No-stop Hedging
concepts.blurb: No-stop hedging is the practice of replacing a stop loss with an offsetting position: when a trade moves against you, instead of exiting, you open an opposite position of equal size in the same…

concepts.name: Optimal F
concepts.blurb: Optimal f is Ralph Vince's position-sizing construction: the fixed fraction of capital that, applied to every trade in a strategy's historical trade list, would have maximized the geometric growth of…

concepts.name: Order Constructs
concepts.blurb: Order constructs are composite orders: arrangements of two or more basic order types linked by management logic.

concepts.name: Order Types
concepts.blurb: Order types are the basic execution instructions a venue accepts.

concepts.name: Pattern-invalidation Stop
concepts.blurb: A pattern-invalidation stop is a stop loss placed at the price where the chart pattern that justified the trade stops being that pattern.

concepts.name: Portfolio-aware Sizing
concepts.blurb: Portfolio-aware sizing sets each position's size with reference to everything else the account already holds, rather than treating every trade as an island.

concepts.name: Profit Target Taxonomy
concepts.blurb: A profit target taxonomy classifies take-profit rules by what the target level is anchored to.

concepts.name: Prop-firm Rule Mechanics

concepts.name: Pyramiding
concepts.blurb: Pyramiding is scaling into a winning position: the trade opens with an initial unit, and further units are added only as price moves favorably and the idea keeps confirming.

concepts.name: Risk of Ruin
concepts.blurb: Risk of ruin is the probability that an account falls to a level from which it cannot, or is not allowed to, continue trading.

concepts.name: R-multiple Framework
concepts.blurb: The R-multiple framework expresses every trade outcome as a multiple of its initial risk.

concepts.name: Scaling Out
concepts.blurb: Scaling out is exiting a position in planned parts rather than all at once: a partial take-profit at the first objective, another at the next, and a final piece, the runner, left to trail for the…

concepts.name: Sizing Bases
concepts.blurb: A sizing base is the reference quantity a position's size is computed from, and naming it is the first decision in any sizing scheme.

concepts.name: Stop-and-reverse

concepts.name: Stop Placement vs Liquidity Pools
concepts.blurb: Stop placement vs liquidity pools is the interaction between where traders park protective stops and where the market finds resting orders to trade against.

concepts.name: Structure Stop
concepts.blurb: A structure stop is placed beyond the chart feature that invalidates the trade: below the swing low a long was built on, beyond the order block or zone that anchored the entry, outside the boundary…

concepts.name: Trailing Method Taxonomy
concepts.blurb: A trailing method taxonomy classifies trailing stops by what the stop follows and how it is allowed to move.

concepts.name: TWAP/VWAP/POV Execution
concepts.blurb: TWAP, VWAP, and POV are the three workhorse execution algorithms for working a large parent order into the market as a stream of smaller child orders.

concepts.name: Volatility Stop
concepts.blurb: A volatility stop is a stop-loss placed a multiple of current volatility away from price, in practice almost always k times the average true range.

concepts.name: Volatility-targeted Sizing
concepts.blurb: Volatility-targeted sizing sets position size from a volatility estimate rather than a hand-placed stop.

concepts.name: Adaptive Parameterization
concepts.blurb: Adaptive parameterization is the design principle of letting an indicator's or strategy's parameters (lookback length, smoothing factor, band width, stop distance) change automatically with measured…

concepts.name: Alerts & Webhooks
concepts.blurb: An alert is a platform notification that fires when a chart condition evaluates true: price crosses a level, an indicator flips state, a breakout confirms.

concepts.name: Alternative Bar Types
concepts.blurb: Alternative bar types replace the clock as the trigger for printing a new bar.

concepts.name: Chart Scales
concepts.blurb: A chart scale is the rule that maps price to vertical distance on a chart.

concepts.name: Composite Oscillators
concepts.blurb: A composite oscillator is a single indicator built by blending several oscillators into one output.

concepts.name: Confluence & Scoring Systems
concepts.blurb: Confluence is the agreement of multiple independent pieces of evidence at the same time and place: trend, momentum, a key level, and a volume signature all pointing the same way.

concepts.name: Cross-instrument Composition
concepts.blurb: Cross-instrument composition is the umbrella for techniques whose input is built from more than one instrument.

concepts.name: Currency-adjusted Charting
concepts.blurb: Currency-adjusted charting re-denominates an instrument's price series into a different currency, so the chart shows what a holder of that currency actually experienced.

concepts.name: Custom Indices/baskets
concepts.blurb: A custom index or basket is a synthetic series built from several instruments and then charted like a single symbol.

concepts.name: EquiVolume
concepts.blurb: EquiVolume is a charting style introduced by Richard W. Arms Jr. in his 1971 book Profits in Volume.

concepts.name: Filter-setup-trigger-exit Architecture
concepts.blurb: Filter-setup-trigger-exit architecture decomposes a rules-based strategy into four layered roles.

concepts.name: Heikin Ashi
concepts.blurb: Heikin Ashi (from Japanese, roughly "average bar") is a chart transform that replaces each candle's actual values with averaged, partly recursive ones.

concepts.name: HTF-level Proximity Filters
concepts.blurb: An HTF-level proximity filter gates lower-timeframe signals by their distance to higher-timeframe levels.

concepts.name: Kagi
concepts.blurb: A Kagi chart is a Japanese price-only chart that ignores time entirely: the line extends vertically while price moves in the current direction and turns only when price reverses by a predefined…

concepts.name: Lead-lag Instrument Triggers
concepts.blurb: Lead-lag instrument triggers are trade signals generated on one instrument from the behavior of a related instrument that tends to move first.

concepts.name: Line Break
concepts.blurb: A line break chart is a Japanese time-independent chart built entirely from closing prices.

concepts.name: MTF Alignment & Confluence Scoring
concepts.blurb: MTF (multi-timeframe) alignment is the practice of evaluating the same condition, such as trend direction, momentum state, or structure bias, on several timeframes at once and reading how many agree.

concepts.name: Point & Figure
concepts.blurb: Point & Figure is a time-independent charting method that records price in alternating columns of X's (rising) and O's (falling).

concepts.name: Ratio/spread Charts
concepts.blurb: A ratio or spread chart replaces a single instrument's price with a synthetic series built from two: a ratio divides one price by another (the gold/silver ratio, a sector ETF over its index, an…

concepts.name: Renko
concepts.blurb: Renko is a price-only chart type that rebuilds the market as a series of fixed-size bricks (from the Japanese renga, brick) instead of time-based bars.

concepts.name: Repaint-safe Engineering
concepts.blurb: Repaint-safe engineering is the discipline of building indicators and signals so that what history shows is what live trading actually displayed.

concepts.name: Signal Hygiene
concepts.blurb: Signal hygiene is the set of engineering rules that turn a raw condition into a signal stream a trader can act on.

concepts.name: Signal Inversion
concepts.blurb: Signal inversion takes a defined signal and trades its opposite: sell where the rule says buy, buy where it says sell.

concepts.name: Strategy Switching & Rotation
concepts.blurb: Strategy switching and rotation is a meta-layer that decides which strategy is allowed to trade, rather than generating entries itself.

concepts.name: Top-down Analysis
concepts.blurb: Top-down analysis is a workflow: establish context on higher timeframes first, then descend to lower timeframes to time the trade.

concepts.name: Trend/range Classifiers
concepts.blurb: A trend/range classifier is any rule or model that labels the market's current state, trending or ranging, so a system can decide which playbook applies.

concepts.name: Volatility Regime Switches
concepts.blurb: A volatility regime switch is a composition rule: measure volatility, classify the reading into a state such as quiet, normal, or stressed, and change the system's behavior when the state changes.

concepts.name: Volume-adjusted Time

concepts.name: Benchmark Comparison Discipline
concepts.blurb: Benchmark comparison discipline is the practice of judging a strategy against the right passive or naive alternative before crediting it with skill.

concepts.name: Bias Taxonomy
concepts.blurb: A bias taxonomy is a structured checklist of the systematic errors that inflate backtested performance: the recurring ways a historical test can flatter a strategy that has no real edge.

concepts.name: CAGR
concepts.blurb: CAGR, the compound annual growth rate, is the single constant yearly rate at which an account would have had to grow to get from its starting value to its ending value over the measured period.

concepts.name: Calmar Ratio
concepts.blurb: The Calmar ratio is a risk-adjusted performance measure that divides a strategy's annualized return by the absolute value of its maximum drawdown over the same period.

concepts.name: Cost-model Realism

concepts.name: Cost Sensitivity
concepts.blurb: Cost sensitivity is the practice of stress-testing a strategy's results against increasing levels of trading friction: commissions, spread, slippage, and fees.

concepts.name: Deflated Sharpe Ratio
concepts.blurb: The deflated Sharpe ratio (DSR) is a test statistic that asks whether a backtested Sharpe ratio is genuinely positive once two inflations are stripped out: the statistical noise in estimating a…

concepts.name: Drawdown Statistics
concepts.blurb: Drawdown statistics describe the declines of an equity curve from its running peak: how deep the losses went, how long they lasted, and how quickly the account recovered.

concepts.name: Expectancy
concepts.blurb: Expectancy is the average amount a strategy makes or loses per trade, taken across the whole distribution of outcomes.

concepts.name: Extended Risk-adjusted Ratios

concepts.name: Forward/paper-trading Confirmation

concepts.name: Information Ratio

concepts.name: In-sample / Out-of-sample Split
concepts.blurb: An in-sample / out-of-sample split partitions historical data into a segment used to build and tune a strategy (in-sample) and a later segment kept untouched until the design is frozen…

concepts.name: Live Decay Tracking

concepts.name: MAE/MFE Distributions
concepts.blurb: MAE/MFE distributions describe how far trades move against and in favor of the entry before they close.

concepts.name: Martin Ratio
concepts.blurb: The Martin ratio, also called the Ulcer Performance Index or return over Ulcer Index, is a risk-adjusted performance measure that divides a strategy's excess return by its Ulcer Index.

concepts.name: Multiple-testing Correction
concepts.blurb: A multiple-testing correction is any statistical adjustment that accounts for how many strategies, parameters, or signals were tried before the reported result was selected.

concepts.name: Parameter Stability
concepts.blurb: Parameter stability is the property that a strategy's performance changes smoothly as its inputs are varied.

concepts.name: Probability of Backtest Overfitting
concepts.blurb: The probability of backtest overfitting (PBO) is a diagnostic that estimates how likely it is that a strategy selected for its backtest performance is actually a poor performer out-of-sample.

concepts.name: Profit Factor
concepts.blurb: Profit factor is the ratio of a strategy's gross profits to its gross losses over a test period: the sum of all winning trades divided by the absolute sum of all losing trades.

concepts.name: Purged Cross-validation

concepts.name: Randomization Tests
concepts.blurb: Randomization tests judge a backtest not against zero but against luck.

concepts.name: Robustness Testing

concepts.name: Sharpe Ratio
concepts.blurb: The Sharpe ratio, introduced by William F. Sharpe in 1966 as the reward-to-variability ratio, measures return per unit of risk: the average return earned in excess of the risk-free rate, divided by…

concepts.name: Significance of Returns
concepts.blurb: Statistical significance of returns is the practice of testing whether a strategy's average return is distinguishable from zero, or from a benchmark, given the noise in the data.

concepts.name: Sortino Ratio
concepts.blurb: The Sortino ratio measures return per unit of downside risk.

concepts.name: SQN
concepts.blurb: The System Quality Number, usually shortened to SQN, is a single score for trading-system quality introduced by trading psychologist Van K. Tharp.

concepts.name: Throughput Stats
concepts.blurb: Throughput stats describe how a strategy uses time and capital rather than how profitable it is: trade frequency, exposure or time-in-market, turnover, average holding time, and capacity.

concepts.name: Walk-forward Analysis
concepts.blurb: Walk-forward analysis is a validation protocol that turns the single in-sample / out-of-sample split into a repeating procedure.

concepts.name: Win Rate
concepts.blurb: Win rate is the percentage of closed trades that finish profitable: winners divided by total trades.
